# Directory to save images

title: Support for different LoRA formats
author: filipstrand
body: As discussed in #40 there are different types of LoRA formats. To keep track of what works and what doesn't I have added a table in the README called [Supported LoRA formats](https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux?tab=readme-ov-file#supported-lora-formats-updated). I am not sure what the best way is to categorize the formats, but I thought this issue can serve as a place for anyone to post what they have tried and if it worked or not, along with any other information. It would also be really interesting to hear from people which are the most common sources for fine-tuning online (e.g like [civitai.com](https://civitai.com/models/train) or [fal.ai](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/flux-lora-fast-training)), so we can prioritize support for these weights.

title: proposals for refactoring/simplify CLI entry points
author: anthonywu
body:
The 3 current executables: `mflux-generate`, `mflux-generate-controlnet`, `mflux-save` and potentially other reasonable additions such as `mflux-webui`, etc will share common args and options.

I propose a refactoring to de-dupe the copy-pasted `parser.add_argument` calls across the N files.

## easy 🔵💊

this is a no-op refactoring of the existing code

1. create a new package `mflux.ui.cli` and new module `mflux.ui.cli.app` where we keep the `argparse.ArgumentParser` objects but "organize" them into composable parsers that can be included in a specific facet of the CLI (i.e. generate vs. generate-controlnet vs save)
2. define parsers where args are grouped by whether they are destined for:
  - `Flux1(...)` # quantize, model paths, lora_{paths,scales}
  - `generate_image(...)`. # prompt, model, steps, guidance, seed, metadata etc
  - feature specific: `controlnet_image_path`, `controlnet_strength`, etc
3. the various executable scripts will
  - `from mflux.ui.cli.app import ModelArgParser, GenerateImageArgParser, ...`
  - for the specific script e.g. `mflux-generate`, instantiate that script's own parser but include the common parser configs using the [`parents=[...]` arg](https://docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html#parents)

this will allow for expansion of the CLI suite without continuing to dupe the similar args

## inconvenient alternatives 🔴💊

1. refactor to something like [Google's `python-fire`](https://github.com/google/python-fire) OR [FastAPI's `typer`](http://typer.tiangolo.com) which will reflect (in the Java-like way) on your methods and auto generate CLIs. With this, you might just need a `cli.py` that provides wrappers to all the underlying functions to call.
2. refactor to [`click`](https://click.palletsprojects.com/en/8.1.x/) and accept the trade-off of additional deps in the core install, but gain the possibility of "free TUI" via [trogon textual terminal ui](https://github.com/Textualize/trogon). Both teams/projects are strong python community contributors so the risk is low/medium to follow their work.

These alternative implementations can easily be community project like `mflux-fire-cli` or `mflux-tui` but it would split the contributor energy a bit. (tbh, I'll start the click/trogon-based `mflux-tui` if no one gets to it before me)

I like these TUIs options over the GUI/webapp implementations because they couple to implementations in a way that's convenient to backend devs, all the while introducing much less code bloat to the core repo.

I expect people will use the newest [Python 3.13](https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html) and try to install mflux and fail. Sharing the latest compat info that I gathered.

# Known blockers

- [x] `torch` needs to provide wheels for macOS Python 3.13 [tracking issue](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/130249)

As of October 10, [torch nightly builds](https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/torch/) shows `*cp312-none-mac*` as the latest matches. We need to wait for `cp313-none-mac` to be available then can test with `pip install --pre torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl`

```

          torch==1.0.0
... snipped ...

      and torch<=1.5.0 has no wheels with a matching Python implementation tag, we can conclude that torch<1.0.1 cannot be used.
      And because torch>=1.5.1 has no wheels with a matching Python ABI tag and you require torch, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

I expect torch to update within a month.

-----

- [x] `mlx`'s CircleCI configs needs to build and distribute wheels for 3.13

As of Oct 10, https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aml-explore%2Fmlx%203.12&type=code shows 3.12 as the newest python versions accounted for.

I have a local git clone of `mlx` that I compiled with `python3.13` and I can get it to install, so I expect this to be resolved soon upstream.

-----

## other libraries

these other libraries do not `pip install` as of Oct 10, but I did not investigate how ready these upstream projects are for 3.13

- [x] `tokenizers` [tracking issue](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/issues/1639)

title: proposal: automatic output file naming
author: anthonywu
body:
Currently the pattern for automatic image naming is `image.*` and the subsequent images are smartly indexed as `image-N.*` etc.

However, I think we can make some improvements:

1. always add the dimensions to the image name like `image-512x512.png`
2. automatically summarize the prompt into a file name - so if you had a prompt about a dog playing in a park, the filename can be summarized by some tool as `dog-play-in-park.*`. The tool can be something traditional/fast like [`nltk`](https://www.nltk.org) or some other modern embedding/ranking tool for finding the most relevant keywords.
3. allow users to opt-in to automatic placeholders such as
  - `{iso_date} ISO date `yyyy-mm-dd`
  - `{unix_timestamp}` via `date +%s` or python str fmt
  - `{seed}`
  - other placeholders that represent the various params: `guidance`, `quantize`, etc

not trying to scope creep on what we support - just enough that every file name can be reasonably expected to be unique (seed and prompt summary, at the minimum)

We can also make a API for a `OutputFileNamer` - we'll provide reasonable defaults, and any users of the library can inject their own customization as needed.

title: A Presumptuous Suggestion: Adding Localized Redraw Based on Image-to-Image (Like Inpainting)
author: raysers
body:
The current flux painting approach involves a high degree of randomness. Tools like LoRA, ControlNet, and image-to-image generation are all aimed at providing users with more control to mitigate this randomness. Therefore, I would like to propose the possibility of adding a “localized redraw” feature based on image-to-image generation:

For example, when users upload a reference image, they could also upload an image mask to overlay on the reference. This could potentially enable the following:

Setting the reference image intensity to 0 within the mask area, allowing flux to freely generate content there, while keeping the reference image intensity at 1 outside the mask, preserving the original details. This would effectively achieve “localized redraw.”

In a generation process filled with randomness, users might find some images broadly satisfying while only disliking certain parts. Allowing the specification of these areas for flux to redraw could significantly enhance user control.

I am not familiar with the mlx code structure, and I don’t know how much effort this feature would require to implement. Therefore, this is merely a suggestion for the official team’s reference.

title: Information Sharing on the rf_inversion Technology
author: raysers
body:
Could I share a new piece of technology information? Recently, I discovered an interesting project called Fluxtapoz:

https://github.com/logtd/ComfyUI-Fluxtapoz

Its initial platform is ComfyUI and is currently only compatible with the non-mlx standard version of flux. However, some enthusiasts have ported it to run within Diffusers:

https://github.com/raven38/rf_inversion

Thus, it may still be possible to adapt it for mflux compatibility.

This technology appears to be distinct from ControlNet and ipadapter. It is rumored that it doesn’t require a model; it can achieve consistent style transfer, style imitation, and similar functions solely through prompt inputs.

However:

At the moment, I don’t have the necessary hardware to run standard flux, so I haven’t tested this technology personally. All my information comes from the official demonstrations and some blogger reviews.

Additionally, I’ve noticed that the current mflux development team seems stretched thin, with only @filipstrand and @anthonywu actively contributing on a regular basis at the moment. (There have been other active contributors in the past, but right now it’s just these two.) Since mlx is relatively new, there are very few who are truly proficient with it. This raises the bar for contributors and understandably limits the available manpower. Therefore, I don’t want to add to the team’s workload by suggesting they put this on their to-do list (which already seems to have an extensive backlog).

I’m merely sharing this brief overview of the technology as a piece of information. The reason for sharing: I think that, given the rapid iteration of new technologies, this could be a short-lived innovation, but it’s also possible that it might become a game-changing technology, alongside ControlNet and ipadapter.

If it turns out to be the latter, then sharing this information will have been worthwhile. Who knows—maybe this mention might even have a bit of foresight? And if one day this technology sparks something remarkable when combined with mflux, wouldn’t that be exciting? Anything is possible, I believe.

title: homebrew Python version &  `uv tool install --upgrade mflux` issue -> documentation note?
author: gmorain
body:
Hi,

I had an issue updating MFlux to 0.5.0 this morning, as the `tool install --upgrade mflux` command failed. 

Homebrew is quite 'aggressive' in keeping all package versions up to date, so after a recent `brew install <something>` my setup was pushed to Python 3.13 (as seen with the `python3 --version` and `uv python list` commands).

Having met this kind of breaking behaviour before, and having seen the Python 3.13 note and issue in the MFlux README / repo, I reverted my default homebrew Python version to 3.9 and voilà! (uv still uses the recommended Python version defined in the toml file coming with mflux (ie something >=3.10 if I am not mistaken).

```bash
brew unlink python@3.9
brew unlink python@3.13
brew link --force --overwrite python@3.9
uv tool install --upgrade mflux
```

Hope this helps people getting the same issue while using homebrew and MFlux

title: Prevent duplicate CLI argument: --quantize
author: azrahello
body:
Hi!
Just a quick heads-up — after creating a new environment today and running mflux-generate-depth, I encountered the following error:

`argparse.ArgumentError: argument --quantize/-q: conflicting option strings: --quantize, -q`

It seems that the --quantize argument is being added more than once, leading to a conflict in argparse.
Strangely, everything worked fine in my previous environment, even after pulling the latest updates with git pull.
For now, I fixed it by commenting out the second call to add_argument() for --quantize inside mflux-generate-depth.
Just wanted to share in case this helps for debugging or for future updates!

title: Remove all PyTorch dependencies for Depth Pro
author: filipstrand
body: Currently, we cheat a little bit and run `torch.nn.functional.interpolate` in `depth_pro.py` and `depth_pro_util.py`. It would be nice to eventually replace these with an MLX equivalent. We have a test case in `test_depth_pro.py` that does a hard-assert on a reference depth map given a fixed input image, so that could be used to ensure correct functionality of a proposed solution. Ideally, a proposed solution would only differ slightly in its output compared to the current one.

title: Feature request: load FLUX models directly from a single `.safetensors` checkpoint
author: zmactep
body:
# Summary

`mflux` is intentionally minimal, yet today it still expects a full Diffusers-style folder hierarchy (transformer/, vae/, text_encoder/, etc.) when loading FLUX weights. Hugging Face already hosts merged checkpoints such as `flux1-schnell.safetensors` (and fp8/nf4 variants) that bundle everything into a single file (e.g. [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/flux1-schnell/blob/main/flux1-schnell-fp8.safetensors)). Adding the ability to load that single file would make installation far simpler for new users.

# Issue

Hi @filipstrand, thanks for the brilliant work on `mflux`! 
That current layout is great for Diffusers, but it’s  “heavy” for users who just want to drop a checkpoint into a folder and run `mflux-generate`. It also duplicates a lot of storage when you keep several quantized variants around.

## Why single-file matters
* **Merged checkpoints already exist.**  
  * `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell` → `flux1-schnell.safetensors` (23 GB)  
  * `Kijai/flux-fp8` → `flux1-schnell-fp8-e4m3fn.safetensors` (~12 GB)  
  * Other NF4 / 4-bit / LoRA-merged flavors, all in one file.  
* Community UIs such as ComfyUI and other MLX demos simply drop that file into `models/unet` – no extra folders needed.
* It matches what Stable-Diffusion users have become accustomed to with `.ckpt`/`.safetensors` files.

## Proposed API
```bash
mflux-generate --checkpoint /path/to/flux1-dev.safetensors [...]
```

Thanks again for `mflux`!

title: ConceptAttention only works for single token concepts
author: filipstrand
body:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c35642ed-e7b4-4fca-8d20-e7034489e6ec)

For "sky" (single token, working well): 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3b3439e-81c9-4b70-97e6-dad96cbcccc8)

For "skyscraper" (multi-token, ['▁sky', 's', 'cra', 'per'], broken):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68c47887-6280-420d-95f5-f8b7087af002)

At least we should warn when user is trying to find a concept that is multi-token.

Potential solution could be averaging over concept tokens somehow 

Some debugging results from cursor: 

```
The Fundamental Problem:
The concept attention system is fundamentally broken for multi-token concepts because:
The system only uses the first token (token index 0) for visualization
For "skyscraper", it's analyzing attention for "sky" instead of the full concept
The remaining tokens ['s', 'cra', 'per'] are completely ignored
This is happening at line 92 in concept_util.py: heatmap = np.array(heatmaps)[0]
Key Insights from Tensor Shapes:
concept_dim = 256: This represents all token positions in the padded sequence
Final shape (256, 32, 32): 256 different token attention maps
Only [0] is used: We're throwing away 255 other potential attention patterns
The system processes all 256 positions but only visualizes the first one
Why This Matters:
Multi-token concepts like "skyscraper", "lighthouse", "butterfly" are effectively treated as their first token
This explains why concept attention seems to work well for single-token concepts but fails for compound words
The attention computation is happening correctly - the visualization is just broken
This is a critical bug that makes the concept attention feature unreliable for a large class of concepts. The fix would be to either:
Average across all relevant concept tokens
Allow users to specify which token to visualize
Show attention for all tokens simultaneously
```

title: Proposal: use fsspec library to widely support file i/o to/from many storage systems
author: anthonywu
body:
# Proposal

Any prompt and input/output image paths should be read/write-able to a wide(r) variety of storages.

# Use [`fsspec` library](https://filesystem-spec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/usage.html)

- it's already installed in the venv as a transitive dependency

```
$ uv pip show fsspec
Name: fsspec
Version: 2025.5.1
Location: /Users/anthonywu/workspace/mflux/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages
Required-by: huggingface-hub, torch
```

- I have used it previously and trust its implementation
- widely used and well maintained project
- if you use any of the implementations, users are responsible for installing their own additional libraries like `boto3` and `pyarrow` to write to the arbitrary destinations

We can keep the paths local by default - so no change to current behavior. Then, if you attach any prefixes like `s3://` or `https://` or anything supported in [fsspec implementations](https://github.com/fsspec/filesystem_spec/tree/master/fsspec/implementations), we let the fsspec take over to fetch the file to a local cache file (or directly to text/Image objects) and we continue the workflow from there.

title: Planning: Type cleanup
author: anthonywu
body:
I want to help do a cleanup of the type hinting debt.

Using the classic `mypy` and the new/upcoming Astral [ty](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty) here's what the two tools flag.

[mypy_snapshot.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20955825/mypy_snapshot.txt)
`Found 528 errors in 144 files (checked 210 source files)`

[ty_snapshot.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20955826/ty_snapshot.txt)
`Found 186 diagnostics`

Because `ty` is in beta for now, using it as the source of correctness is probably not a good idea, so my proposal is to get to a checkpoint where `mypy` reports no warnings/errors.

Due to the expected bloat of the fixer changes, I think the cleanup should be done in multiple PRs, each focusing on a specific pattern or a specific collection of files, in order to make reviews easier.

Checking with @filipstrand to see if he agrees it's worthwhile to get `mypy` (and later `ty check` errors down to 0, then we can introduce `pre-commit` hooks to enforce.

title: open discussion: mflux-extras, affiliated libraries
author: anthonywu
body:
One thing I like about libraries is the good ones are well scoped, the authors decide what's in and what's out of scope as a guideline to continual development.

One way `mflux` embodied this spirit from the beginning was to not rely on `torch` or `diffusers`, and lean into relying on MLX. Another way we've held the line is keeping some scripts in the tools dir but not officially part of the mflux package. This ensures the library does not mission creep.

However, this conflicts with the maintainers/users desire of ever expanding feature sets such as:

- Gradio GUI
- RESTful API
- DALLE-compatible endpoints
- ComfyUI integration points
- Upscale using a specific controlnet model (implemented)
- Turbo using a specific third party model (postponed)

My proposal is we could:

1. shove all of these into an additional package called `mflux-extras` and import as either `mflux_extras` or with some [namespaced packages setup](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/packaging-namespace-packages/) we can make `mflux.extras` but publish separately. (or multiple packages, `mflux-workflows`, `mflux-servers`, and `mflux-mcp` which I'm working on)
2. `mflux` will have dependency groups including a `extras` for `pip install mflux[extras]` for when users want all the bells and whistles (but acknowledge venv bloat and potential install conflicts)
3. all affiliated packages will publish CLI tools under the `mflux` top level namespace, and `mflux-` prefix as CLIs

I can volunteer to bootstrap all the new github repos and pypi artifacts, it's actually not that big of an effort.

title: Support Qwen Image Edit 2511
author: filipstrand
body:
Qwen Image Edit 2511 was recently merged to diffusers. 

Should add this for the next release too once SeedVR2 work is done.

Some naming conventions probably have to be updated on our side since we dropped support for the first Edit model and currently default to 2509. Since a lot of investment with LoRAs and similar have been made with the 2509 model, my initial feeling says that we should support both 2509 and 2511 going forward.

title: Wrong placement of model weights when also specifying a LoRA
author: filipstrand
body:
When running the following command from a fresh install 

```
mflux-generate-qwen-edit \
  --image-paths "monkey.png" \
  --prompt "将镜头极度拉近，使用超长焦镜头进行极端特写拍摄，主体占据画面的大部分空间，背景完全虚化，营造出强烈的视觉冲击力和亲密感。Extreme zoom in with a super telephoto lens, creating an intense close-up where the subject dominates most of the frame, with the background completely blurred, creating a strong visual impact and sense of intimacy." \
  --steps 8 \
  --guidance 2.5 \
  --width 1024 \
  --height 1024 \
  --lora-paths "lightx2v/Qwen-Image-Lightning" "dx8152/Qwen-Edit-2509-Multiple-angles" \
  --lora-scales 0.5 1.0
```

It places the model in the mflux cache instead of the hugging face cache (probably because we also include a LoRA in the same command).

title: mflux-generate-z-image-turbo takes twice of VRAM at the end of generation
author: zaskara
body:
First — thanks to filipstrand and contributors!

title: Klein 9B crashes with shape mismatch — Qwen3TextEncoder always uses 4B defaults
author: James-Christensen
body:
Flux2Klein with ModelConfig.flux2_klein_9b() fails during text encoding with:

ValueError: [broadcast_shapes] Shapes (2560) and (1,512,4096) cannot be broadcast.

The crash occurs in Qwen3VLRMSNorm.__call__ because the Qwen3TextEncoder is always constructed with default parameters (matching the 4B text encoder), even when using the 9B model config.

Root cause:

In flux2_initializer.py, _init_models passes transformer_overrides to the transformer but hardcodes the text encoder with no overrides:

def _init_models(model) -> None:
    model.vae = Flux2VAE()
    model.transformer = Flux2Transformer(**model.model_config.transformer_overrides)
    model.text_encoder = Qwen3TextEncoder()  # <-- always uses defaults (hidden_size=2560)

The 9B model's text encoder weights (from HuggingFace) have hidden_size=4096 and intermediate_size=12288, but the encoder is constructed with the 4B defaults (hidden_size=2560, intermediate_size=9728). The weights load successfully (since weight application doesn't validate shapes), but the first forward pass crashes on the dimension mismatch.

Reproduction:

Via CLI (uv tool install mflux):

mflux-generate-flux2 \
  --model flux2-klein-9b \
  --prompt "a cat" \
  --steps 4 \
  --seed 42 \
  --width 1024 \
  --height 1024

Via Python API:

from mflux.models.common.config import ModelConfig
from mflux.models.flux2.variants import Flux2Klein

model = Flux2Klein(model_config=ModelConfig.flux2_klein_9b())
image = model.generate_image(
    seed=42,
    prompt="a cat",
    num_inference_steps=4,
)

Both produce:

ValueError: [broadcast_shapes] Shapes (2560) and (1,512,4096) cannot be broadcast.

Note: flux2-klein-4b works fine from the same installation, since the Qwen3TextEncoder defaults happen to match the 4B text encoder dimensions.

Text encoder configs from HuggingFace:

Parameter | 4B (default) | 9B (needed) -- | -- | -- hidden_size | 2560 | 4096 intermediate_size | 9728 | 12288 num_hidden_layers | 36 | 36 num_attention_heads | 32 | 32 num_key_value_heads | 8 | 8

Proposed fix:

Add a text_encoder_overrides field to ModelConfig (mirroring transformer_overrides), populate it for the 9B config, and pass it through in the initializer:

  1. In model_config.py, add text_encoder_overrides: dict | None = None to ModelConfig.__init__ and add the overrides to the flux2-klein-9b entry:

    "flux2-klein-9b": ModelConfig(
    ...
    text_encoder_overrides={
        "hidden_size": 4096,
        "intermediate_size": 12288,
    },
),

  2. In flux2_initializer.py, change:

    model.text_encoder = Qwen3TextEncoder()

    to:

    model.text_encoder = Qwen3TextEncoder(**model.model_config.text_encoder_overrides)

The 4B model is unaffected since its text_encoder_overrides defaults to {}.

Environment:

  • mflux v0.15.5
  • macOS, Apple Silicon
  • Python 3.12 (CLI via uv tool) and Python 3.14.3 (API via pip install)

title: Z-Image training preview images ignore `guidance` parameter from config
author: azrahello
body:
# Bug: Z-Image training preview images ignore `guidance` parameter from config

## Description

When training a LoRA on `z-image` (non-turbo) with `guidance` set in the training config JSON, the preview images generated during training always use `guidance=0.0` instead of the configured value. This results in preview images that do not accurately represent the actual training progress, since Z-Image standard relies on Classifier-Free Guidance for quality output.

## Root Cause

In `z_image_training_adapter.py`, the `generate_preview_image` method calls `self._z.generate_image()` without passing the `guidance` parameter:

```python
def generate_preview_image(self, *, seed, prompt, width, height, steps, image_paths=None):
    with self._assistant_disabled():
        return self._z.generate_image(
            seed=seed, prompt=prompt, num_inference_steps=steps, height=height, width=width
        )
```

Since `guidance` is not passed, `generate_image` receives `guidance=None`, which is then converted to `0.0` in `Config.__init__`:

```python
self._guidance = 0.0 if guidance is None else float(guidance)
```

With `guidance=0.0`, `_encode_prompts` skips negative encoding entirely (`if guidance <= 1.0: return text_encodings, None`), so no CFG is applied.

## Why it only affects Z-Image (non-turbo)

Z-Image Turbo has `supports_guidance=False` in its `ModelConfig`, so `generate_image` forces `guidance=0.0` regardless — the bug is invisible. Z-Image standard has `supports_guidance=True` and requires CFG (`guidance > 1.0`) for proper generation quality.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a training config with `"model": "z-image"` and `"guidance": 5.0`
2. Start training with `mflux-train`
3. Observe that preview images are generated with `guidance=0.0` (visible in the output metadata or by comparing quality with a manually generated image using `guidance=5.0`)

## Suggested Fix

Cache the `guidance` value from the training spec and pass it to `generate_image`:

```python
class ZImageTrainingAdapter(TrainingAdapter):
    def __init__(self, *, model_config: ModelConfig, quantize: int | None):
        self._model_config = model_config
        self._z = ZImage(quantize=quantize, model_config=model_config)
        self._guidance: float | None = None

    def create_config(self, training_spec: TrainingSpec, *, width: int, height: int) -> Config:
        if self._guidance is None and training_spec.guidance is not None:
            self._guidance = training_spec.guidance
        return Config(
            model_config=self._model_config,
            num_inference_steps=training_spec.steps,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            guidance=training_spec.guidance,
        )

    def generate_preview_image(self, *, seed, prompt, width, height, steps, image_paths=None):
        with self._assistant_disabled():
            return self._z.generate_image(
                seed=seed, prompt=prompt, num_inference_steps=steps, height=height, width=width,
                guidance=self._guidance,
            )
```

Alternatively, the `generate_preview_image` protocol in `TrainingAdapter` could be extended to accept a `guidance` parameter, propagated from the trainer.

## Environment

- mflux version: 0.16.2
- Model: `z-image` (Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image)
- Hardware: Apple M2 Ultra, 64GB

title: `is_m1_or_m2()` compile check is too broad
author: azrahello
body:
mx.compile` check penalizes M1/M2 Max and Ultra variants

### Problem

The `is_m1_or_m2()` check introduced in v0.16.1 (#344) disables `mx.compile` on the predict wrapper for **all** M1 and M2 chips. This is too broad — it groups M2 base (8 GPU cores, 8GB) with M2 Ultra (76 GPU cores, 192GB), even though high-end variants behave differently.

### Benchmark Results (Apple M2 Ultra 76-core GPU, 64GB, MLX 0.30.6)

All tests: 1024×1024, 3 runs each.

**Z-Image-Turbo (6B)**

| Quantization | No Compile (warm) | Compile (warm) | Speedup |
|-------------|-------------------|----------------|---------|
| Q4, 8 steps | 40.13s | 39.70s | **1.01×** |
| Full, 8 steps | 39.06s | 38.69s | **1.01×** |

**FLUX.2 Klein (9B)**

| Quantization | No Compile (warm) | Compile (warm) | Speedup |
|-------------|-------------------|----------------|---------|
| Q4, 4 steps | 65.68s | 65.16s | **1.01×** |

**Robust test — Klein 9B Full Precision (alternating A-B pattern, 6 runs each, warmup discarded)**

| Metric | No Compile | Compile | Speedup |
|--------|-----------|---------|---------|
| Median | 23.76s | 23.53s | **1.010×** |
| Min | 23.74s | 23.51s | **1.010×** |
| Std dev | 2.56s | 4.17s | — |

**Training preview generation (Z-Image Q4 832×1248, 5 steps, 270 LoRA layers rank 32 + assistant LoRA)**

| Metric | No Compile | Compile | Speedup |
|--------|-----------|---------|---------|
| Warm avg | 27.94s | 26.34s | **1.06×** |
| First run | 32.38s | 26.51s | **1.22×** |

In **no test case** was `mx.compile` slower on M2 Ultra. The training preview context shows the most benefit (6% warm, 22% first run), likely because the additional LoRA layers give the compiler more graph optimization opportunities.

### Suggested Fix

Exclude Max and Ultra variants from the check, since they have significantly more GPU cores and memory bandwidth than base/Pro models:

```python
@classmethod
def is_m1_or_m2(cls) -> bool:
    if platform.system() != "Darwin":
        return False
    if platform.machine() not in {"arm64", "aarch64"}:
        return False
    chip_name = cls._get_chip_name().lower()
    # Max/Ultra variants benefit from mx.compile
    if "ultra" in chip_name or "max" in chip_name:
        return False
    return "apple m1" in chip_name or "apple m2" in chip_name
```

title: Optimizer state offload for `low_ram` preview generation
author: azrahello
body:
### Problem

When training with `low_ram: true` at higher resolutions (e.g. 1024×1024) with many LoRA layers (270 layers, rank 32), preview image generation causes heavy swap usage (40GB+ on a 64GB system). This is because the optimizer state (AdamW moments m and v) remains in memory while the preview generation needs to run a full inference pass through the transformer + VAE decode.

### Solution

When `low_ram: true` is set, offload the optimizer state to a temporary file on disk before generating previews, then restore it after:

```python
@staticmethod
def _generate_previews_with_offload(adapter, training_spec, training_state):
    optimizer = training_state.optimizer

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        # 1. Save optimizer state to disk
        offload_path = Path(tmp_dir) / "optimizer_offload.safetensors"
        optimizer.save(offload_path)

        # 2. Release from memory
        optimizer.optimizer.state = []
        gc.collect()
        mx.clear_cache()

        # 3. Generate previews with freed memory
        TrainingTrainer._generate_previews(adapter, training_spec, training_state)

        # 4. Restore optimizer state
        restored_state = tree_unflatten(list(mx.load(str(offload_path)).items()))
        optimizer.optimizer.state = restored_state

    gc.collect()
    mx.clear_cache()
```

In the training loop, only the `low_ram` path uses the offload:

```python
if training_state.should_generate_image(training_spec):
    if training_spec.low_ram:
        TrainingTrainer._generate_previews_with_offload(adapter, training_spec, training_state)
    else:
        TrainingTrainer._generate_previews(adapter, training_spec, training_state)
```

### Properties

- **Zero impact on training results** — the optimizer state is saved and restored bit-for-bit via safetensors
- **Negligible I/O overhead** — LoRA optimizer moments are small (hundreds of MB), SSD write/read is milliseconds
- **Only active with `low_ram: true`** — normal training path is untouched
- **Reduces swap pressure significantly** during preview generation at higher resolutions

### Environment

- **Chip**: Apple M2 Ultra (76 GPU cores, 64GB unified memory)
- **MLX**: 0.30.6
- **mflux**: 0.16.1

title: [Feature(s)] Sigma schedules, aspect ratios, shift override, MCF sampler for Z-Image
author: terribilissimo
body:
My PR: https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux/pull/353

## New flags/args

- --shift: override automatic sigma shift (mu) for both schedulers
- --mcf-max-change: MCF sampler that clamps per-step latent changes
- --cosine / --karras / --exponential: alternative sigma schedules
- --aspect: aspect ratio presets with auto-dimension computation
- --saveinfo: descriptive filenames encoding generation parameters
- _All features apply to mflux-generate-z-image-turbo and mflux-generate-z-image_
- **NOTE: when no fork-specific flags are used, behavior is identical to upstream**

## Summary

This PR adds several quality-of-life enhancements to the Z-Image and Z-Image Turbo
pipelines, ported from our zima.py CUDA/PyTorch scripts. All features are
**opt-in** — when none of the new flags are used, behavior is **identical to upstream**.

## New CLI Flags

### Noise Schedule Control
- `--shift <float>` — Override the automatic sigma shift (mu) value.
  By default mu is computed from image dimensions. Higher values push the
  noise schedule towards higher noise levels.
- `--cosine` — Smooth S-curve sigma schedule (more steps at high/low noise)
- `--karras` — Karras schedule with rho=7 (concentrates steps on fine details)
- `--exponential` — Log-spaced sigmas between sigma_max and sigma_min
  (_Only one of the three can be used at a time; mutually exclusive group_)

### Sampling
- `--mcf-max-change <float>` — MCF (Mean Change Factor) sampler that clamps
  per-step latent changes to prevent sudden jumps. Typical: 0.05–0.50, min/max 0.01/1.00.

### Convenience
- `--aspect <preset>` — Aspect ratio presets (1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 16:9,
  9:16, 18:9, 9:18, 21:9, 9:21). **If combined with only `--width` or `--height`,
  the missing dimension is auto-computed and rounded to multiples of 16.**
- `--saveinfo` — Save images with descriptive filenames encoding
  timestamp, seed, steps, LoRA, scheduler, and sigma schedule info
  (convenient, you won't have to look at the EXIF or json for quick reproducibility).

## Modified Files
- `src/mflux/cli/parser/parsers.py` — New args, aspect ratio dict, sigma_schedule resolution; removed `--metadata`
- `src/mflux/models/common/config/config.py` — `sigma_schedule` property
- `src/mflux/models/common/schedulers/linear_scheduler.py` — `_generate_base_sigmas()`
- `src/mflux/models/common/schedulers/flow_match_euler_discrete_scheduler.py` — same
- `src/mflux/models/z_image/variants/z_image.py` — New params in `generate_image()`
- `src/mflux/models/z_image/cli/z_image_turbo_generate.py` — Passthrough + saveinfo
- `src/mflux/models/z_image/cli/z_image_generate.py` — Same
- All CLI entry points (flux, flux2, qwen, z_image, fibo) — Removed `export_json_metadata=args.metadata`

## Testing
All features tested on Apple Silicon (M-series) with both `mflux-generate-z-image-turbo`
and `mflux-generate-z-image`. Baseline output is pixel-identical to upstream when
no new flags are used. See TESTING-SCRIPT.txt for the full test matrix (18 tests).

## Checklist
- [x] No new dependencies added
- [x] All sigma schedule math uses pure MLX (`mx.array`, `mx.cos`, `mx.linspace`)
- [x] Backward-compatible — default behavior unchanged
- [x] Passes existing tests
- [x] Both Z-Image and Z-Image Turbo entry points updated

title: Design review and discussion: MFLUX v1.0 API and CLI
author: filipstrand
body:
As the project has evolved and now support a whole family of models and techniques, the current CLI starts to feel outdated and unnecessarily complex. This is a place to discuss how a new and modern interface could/should look like given what we know about model families, variants and features in 2026 and beyond. 

- Which top level commands should we support (like `mflux generate`, `mflux edit`, `mflux save` etc?)
- What are good names (e.g --image or --images might be preferred to "--image_paths")?
- How should model families be specified? 
- How should model variants be specified (4b, 7b)? 
- How should LoRAs be specified (some cleanups and redesign have already been made here, e.g how we fetch from HF where the repo might include several .safetensors files etc). 
- How should resolution be specified or inferred (via input image, via aspect ratio, default values etc?) 
- How should low-ram optimisations be specified (e.g, what should be hidden behind a single --low-ram vs treated as separate, e.g see. https://github.com/filipstrand/mflux/pull/351) 
- what is natural to have to specify given that we already have an input image in some case (e.g default resolution could be inferred if not specified)
- anticipate/consider what could be coming in the future (e.g more optimisations, other model types etc). 
- how do we document this for humans?
- how do we document this for agents?
- many more things...

I invite everyone to participate in this open discussion, there are no right or wrong answers :) 

I think the more we can share how we use the project currently, and how we wish things to be, the better shot we have at designing a stable and good CLI for the future.  

Once we agree on a design, I think the actual implementation should be fairly trivial with the help of coding agents. 

I'll update this doc with some of my own suggestions after finishing current ongoing work with model porting...

title: flux.2 latent encoding drops 16 pixel strips
author: percontation
body:
When using mflux-generate-flux2-edit to edit one base image, the image looses a strip of 16 pixels from the right and from the bottom. The output image ends up being stretched to cover those 16 pixels.

This is using images whose height and width are both multiples of 16 pixels, and this whole issue doesn't occur when using flux.2 klein via huggingface diffusers.

The mis-scaling should be readily apparent when asking for a small edit to a small photo, and flipping back and forth between the original and the edit. But, here's an artificial example that highlights that content is being cut off:

```bash
mflux-generate-flux2 --model flux2-klein-9b --prompt 'Solid white, with a triple-lined black border' --output /tmp/bordertest.png --height 80 --width 80 --seed 0 # this works fine
mflux-generate-flux2-edit --model flux2-klein-9b --prompt 'change black lines to red' --image-paths /tmp/bordertest.png --output /tmp/bordertest2.png --seed 0 # the border has been cut off from the bottom and right
mflux-generate-flux2 --model flux2-klein-9b --prompt 'frame' --image-path /tmp/bordertest.png --output /tmp/bordertest3.png --seed 0 --image-strength 0.8 # same issue, just using a different conditioning codepath.

title: Calling mflux as a library from mlx-openai-server for flux2 klein 4b to edit results in TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for %: 'NoneType' and 'int'
author: TheOrsa
body:
**Issue type**: Bug

**Description**: Configuring OpenWebUI to call a mlx-openai-server to run image edit with flux2 is not possible in the latest 0.16.8 version.
How to reproduce: Configure an Image edit endpoint in OpenWebUI and try to use it.

**Expected**: Image is uploaded and the prompt is used to return an edited image.

**Actual**: OpenWebUI gives an error for the "backend" 500 (which is mlx-openai-server). The logs on mlx-openai-server show the following:
`TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for %: 'NoneType' and 'int'`

**Additional Info and specially for agents**: This is a type of bug introduced by coding new software and missing some safeguards. The error message is very typical of python at runtime (such as the infamous .NET dll not found exceptions, totally unrelated). In this case, the error means the code is trying to compute the modulo of 2 variables, but one of them was null. Having this as knowledge, I scanned the repository for operations using the modulo operator '%' (this is a brute-force approach I've used in the past where I know the pattern introducing the bug, and its doable on small codebases. The proper approach is to setup a python debugging session but Im unfamiliar with it). I did a codebase search for the '%' in python files, filtered out comment lines, and filtered out the ones containing width or height as operators on the left, which returned the single line causing the exception. I hope this helps for agents and in general the fix is avoiding running the modulo operation without first checking for nulls. What happens over nulls is specific to the surrounding code and the calling function, but usually calling a function to obtain the correct value or sometimes setting it to 0 would at least remove the exception, although the behavior could not throw any error yet be unexpected output (in this case for example it could be an empty image).

title: Support for ModelScope/PEFT LoRA Key Naming
author: s-junjie
body:
ModelScope-trained Lora's are not applied, the CLI reports **0 layers matched** even though the LoRA file is successfully loaded. I made a patch to my app, but thought it would be better to include the fix in mflux directly. 

I used this sample Lora to test: https://www.modelscope.ai/models/OldBoy/lingerie-model-Z-Image-Turbo-Tongyi-MAI-v1.0/summary?version=20260111134817

Below is information for agent reference:

---

## Description
Currently, `mflux` fails to load LoRA adapters exported from ModelScope or trained using the HuggingFace PEFT library. The loader reports "0 layers matched" even when the LoRA file is valid and correctly formatted for the base model.

## Root Cause
The `LoRALoader._match_pattern` method in `mflux/models/common/lora/mapping/lora_loader.py` uses exact string comparison between the safetensors weight keys and the expected model patterns.

PEFT-based LoRAs (very common on ModelScope) append an adapter name (usually `.default`) to the weight keys, which causes the exact match to fail.

### Key Comparison
| Source | Weight Key Example |
|---|---|
| **mflux expects** | `layers.0.attention.to_q.lora_A.weight` |
| **ModelScope/PEFT** | `layers.0.attention.to_q.lora_A.default.weight` |

## Proposed Fix
Update `LoRALoader._match_pattern` to normalize keys by stripping the `.default` segment (and the `.weight` suffix if present) before performing the pattern match.

### Suggested Implementation
```python
    @staticmethod
    def _match_pattern(weight_key: str, pattern: str) -> int | None:
        # Normalize ModelScope/PEFT keys
        normalized_key = weight_key
        if ".default.weight" in normalized_key:
            normalized_key = normalized_key.replace(".default.weight", ".weight")
        elif normalized_key.endswith(".default"):
            normalized_key = normalized_key[:-8]

        if "{block}" in pattern:
            numbers_in_key = re.findall(r"\d+", normalized_key)
            for num_str in numbers_in_key:
                test_block_idx = int(num_str)
                concrete_pattern = pattern.replace("{block}", str(test_block_idx))
                if normalized_key == concrete_pattern:
                    return test_block_idx
            return None
        else:
            return 0 if normalized_key == pattern else None
```

title: Incompatible protobuf constraint (<6.0) conflicts with mlx-audio (requires >=6.33.5)
author: LangeRobert
body:
### Description

Hi, thanks for the great work on `mflux`!

I ran into a dependency resolution issue when trying to use `mflux` together with `mlx-audio`. The problem seems to be caused by incompatible `protobuf` version constraints.

Currently:

* `mflux (>=0.17.1,<0.18.0)` requires
  `protobuf >=4.25.0,<6.0`
* `mlx-audio (>=0.4.2,<0.5.0)` requires
  `protobuf >=6.33.5`

Because of this, dependency resolvers (e.g. Poetry, uv, pip resolver) cannot find a compatible set of packages.

---

### Reproduction

Using Poetry:

```toml
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.11"
mflux = ">=0.17.1,<0.18.0"
mlx-audio = "^0.4.2"
```

Running:

```bash
poetry lock
```

Results in:

```
version solving failed:
mflux requires protobuf <6.0
mlx-audio requires protobuf >=6.33.5
→ no compatible solution
```

---

### Possible solutions

* Relax the constraint to:

  ```text
  protobuf >=4.25.0,<7.0
  ```

title: Feature Request: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Support
author: CodeAndCanvas728
body:
## Summary

Add SD3.5 (Large, Medium, and Turbo variants) as a new model family in MFLUX.

## Motivation

SD3.5 remains one of the most popular open diffusion models, particularly for users who prefer its aesthetic (natural skin tones, cinematic colour, painterly quality) over FLUX's sharper, more detailed output. On Apple Silicon, the only tool that previously supported local SD3.5 inference via MLX was DiffusionKit — which was [[archived in March 2026](https://github.com/argmaxinc/DiffusionKit)](https://github.com/argmaxinc/DiffusionKit) with several open bugs, including [[broken img2img on quantized models](https://github.com/argmaxinc/DiffusionKit/issues/42)](https://github.com/argmaxinc/DiffusionKit/issues/42).

There is currently no actively maintained way to run SD3.5 locally on Mac in native MLX. MFLUX is the natural home for this — it already supports the closely related FLUX architecture, has working img2img and quantization infrastructure, and follows the same line-by-line-from-Diffusers philosophy that would make SD3.5 a clean addition.

## Architecture overlap with existing MFLUX code

SD3.5 and FLUX share significant architectural DNA — both are flow-matching transformers using MMDiT blocks, 16-channel VAEs, and CLIP + T5 text encoding. Key differences:

| Component | FLUX (already in MFLUX) | SD3.5 (to add) |
|-----------|------------------------|----------------|
| **Transformer** | 19 dual-stream + 38 single-stream blocks | 38 pure dual-stream blocks (Large) / 24 (Medium) |
| **Text encoders** | CLIP-L + T5-XXL | CLIP-L + OpenCLIP bigG + T5-XXL |
| **Conditioning** | Pooled CLIP-L via AdaLN | Pooled CLIP-L + CLIP-G via AdaLN |
| **VAE** | 16-ch AutoencoderKL | 16-ch AutoencoderKL (different weights, no post-quant conv) |
| **Scheduler** | Flow matching (Euler discrete) | Flow matching (Euler discrete), different shift |
| **Parameters** | ~12B | ~8B (Large) / ~2B (Medium) |

MFLUX's dual-stream MMDiT blocks are essentially the same as SD3.5's `JointBlock`. The main new component is the **OpenCLIP bigG** text encoder and the triple-encoder conditioning pipeline.

## Reference implementation

Stability AI provides a clean, MIT-licensed reference at [`[Stability-AI/sd3.5](https://github.com/Stability-AI/sd3.5)`](https://github.com/Stability-AI/sd3.5) — just 4 Python files:

- `mmditx.py` — Core MMDiT-X transformer (915 lines)
- `sd3_impls.py` — Pipeline wrapper, VAE encoder/decoder, CFG, sampling
- `other_impls.py` — CLIP-L, CLIP-G, T5 text encoders
- `dit_embedder.py` — Patch and timestep embeddings

## Proposed scope

**Phase 1 — txt2img for SD3.5 Large** (initial PR)
- OpenCLIP bigG encoder in MLX
- Triple text encoder conditioning pipeline
- MMDiT-X transformer (adapted from existing dual-stream blocks)
- Weight loader for HuggingFace SD3.5 safetensors
- SD3.5 VAE weights
- CLI: `mflux-generate-sd3`

**Phase 2 — img2img + quantization** (follow-up PR)
- Leverage existing MFLUX img2img and quantization infra
- Explicitly test and document that quantized img2img works (this was the [[DiffusionKit bug](https://github.com/argmaxinc/DiffusionKit/issues/42)](https://github.com/argmaxinc/DiffusionKit/issues/42) that was never fixed)

**Phase 3 — Medium + Turbo variants** (follow-up PR)
- Config-level changes (depth=24 for Medium, shift/steps for Turbo)

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is SD3.5 a model family you'd want in MFLUX, or is the project intentionally scoped to newer architectures?
2. Any preferences on directory structure? I'd follow the existing `src/mflux/models/sd3/` pattern.
3. The OpenCLIP bigG encoder is the one entirely new network component — should it live in a shared location (since future models might use it) or be scoped to the SD3 model directory?

Happy to start with a draft PR if there's interest.

title: mflux-generate-z-image-turbo crashes over SSH on Mac Mini
author: bobosola
body:
I have OpenClaw on a separate dedicated PC. I am trying to use it to make images with `mflux` on my Mac over a dedicated SSH user account into a shared folder on the Mac. It seems though that the `mflux` code is doing a battery check and then crashing as described below? This is a pretty niche issue but I thought you should know about it. Here's how Kimi k2.5 reported it:

## Environment

- **Device:** Mac Mini (desktop, no battery)
- **OS:** macOS
- **Connection:** SSH session
- **Installation:** mflux installed via `uv tool install mflux`
- **Python:** 3.10

## Command

```bash
mflux-generate-z-image-turbo \
  --model Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo \
  --steps 9 \
  --width 960 \
  --height 544 \
  --prompt "test" \
  --output test.png
```

## Error

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'system_profiler'
```

## Full Traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/openclaw/.local/bin/mflux-generate-z-image-turbo", line 10, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
  File ".../mflux/models/z_image/cli/z_image_turbo_generate.py", line 48, in main
    image = model.generate_image(...)
  File ".../mflux/models/z_image/variants/z_image.py", line 100, in generate_image
    ctx.before_loop(latents)
  File ".../mflux/callbacks/generation_context.py", line 35, in before_loop
    subscriber.call_before_loop(...)
  File ".../mflux/callbacks/instances/battery_saver.py", line 24, in call_before_loop
    current_pct = self._get_battery_percentage()
  File ".../mflux/callbacks/instances/battery_saver.py", line 32, in _get_battery_percentage
    if not self._is_machine_battery_powered():
  File ".../mflux/callbacks/instances/battery_saver.py", line 57, in _is_machine_battery_powered
    machine_model = cls._get_machine_model()
  File ".../mflux/callbacks/instances/battery_saver.py", line 65, in _get_machine_model
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["system_profiler", "SPPowerDataType", "-json"],
        ...
    )
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'system_profiler'
```

## Root Cause

The `battery_saver.py` callback calls `system_profiler` to check if the machine is battery-powered. This fails because:

1. `system_profiler` is not available in SSH sessions (it's a GUI tool)
2. The code doesn't handle `FileNotFoundError` gracefully
3. The check is unnecessary on desktop Macs (Mac Mini, iMac, Mac Studio, Mac Pro)

## Location in Code

`mflux/callbacks/instances/battery_saver.py` line 65:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["system_profiler", "SPPowerDataType", "-json"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=True
)
```

## Suggested Fix

Wrap the `subprocess.run()` call in a try/except block. If `system_profiler` is not found or fails, assume the machine is not battery-powered and continue:

```python
try:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["system_profiler", "SPPowerDataType", "-json"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True
    )
    # ... process result ...
except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
    # system_profiler not available (SSH session) or failed
    # Assume desktop machine (not battery powered)
    return False
```

## Workarounds Attempted

- Using `-B 0` flag to disable battery checking - **did not work**
- Running locally instead of SSH - **would work but not ideal**

## Impact

- Prevents using z-image-turbo models over SSH
- Affects all desktop Mac users running mflux remotely

## Additional Notes

- Regular `mflux-generate` (schnell/dev models) works fine over SSH
- Issue is specific to z-image-turbo variant

title: Enable VAE tiling for FLUX.2 Klein to reduce peak memory ~50%
author: TimPietruskyRunPod
body:
## Problem

FLUX.2 Klein image generation at 1024x1024 uses ~14 GB peak memory on Apple Silicon, even though the model weights are only ~4.4 GB (4-bit quantized). Profiling reveals the VAE decode is the bottleneck — **not** attention or the transformer:

| Pipeline stage | Memory overhead |
|---|---|
| **VAE decode** | **9,629 MB (100% of overhead)** |
| Denoising (transformer) | 1,550 MB |
| Text encoding | 1,106 MB |

This makes FLUX.2 Klein unusable on 8 GB Macs and tight on 16 GB machines.

Model used: [RunPod/FLUX.2-klein-4B-mflux-4bit](https://huggingface.co/RunPod/FLUX.2-klein-4B-mflux-4bit)

## Solution

mflux already has `VAETiler.decode_image_tiled()` with cosine-blended overlap — it's used for video models (SeedVR2, Fibo) but not wired into FLUX.2 Klein or other image models.

Wrapping `Flux2VAE.decode_packed_latents` with tiled decoding (512x512 tiles, 64px overlap) produces identical results with dramatically less memory:

| Metric | Standard | Tiled (512x512) | Tiled (256x256) |
|---|---|---|---|
| VAE decode overhead | 9,629 MB | 2,780 MB | 1,930 MB |
| **Total peak** | **14,032 MB** | **7,178 MB** | **6,326 MB** |
| Generation speed | ~15s/step | ~15s/step | ~15s/step |

**49% peak memory reduction with no speed or quality loss.**

## Proof of concept

This minimal monkey-patch is all it takes:

```python
import mlx.core as mx
from mflux.models.flux2.model.flux2_vae.vae import Flux2VAE
from mflux.models.common.vae.vae_tiler import VAETiler

def decode_packed_latents_tiled(self, packed_latents):
    if packed_latents.ndim == 5:
        packed_latents = packed_latents[:, :, 0, :, :]
    bn_mean = self.bn.running_mean.reshape(1, -1, 1, 1)
    bn_std = mx.sqrt(self.bn.running_var.reshape(1, -1, 1, 1) + self.bn.eps)
    latents = packed_latents * bn_std + bn_mean
    latents = Flux2VAE._unpatchify_latents(latents)
    latent_5d = latents[:, :, None, :, :]

    def decode_fn(tile):
        return self.decode(tile)[:, :, None, :, :]

    return VAETiler.decode_image_tiled(
        latent=latent_5d,
        decode_fn=decode_fn,
        tile_size=(512, 512),
        tile_overlap=(64, 64),
        spatial_scale=8,
    )

Flux2VAE.decode_packed_latents = decode_packed_latents_tiled
```

## Suggestion

Could this be added as a built-in option? E.g.:
- A `--vae-tiling` flag (or enabled by default when resolution ≥ 1024)
- Or as part of `--low-ram` mode

This would benefit all FLUX.2 Klein users on Mac, especially those with 8-16 GB unified memory.

## Environment
- Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB unified memory
- mflux latest (via pip)

title: Expose latents with some extra functionality
author: pericalypsis
body:
This is a feature request, but I can't seem to add that label to the issue.

It would be great to accept and return latents. One common use-case is when you want to use a different model as a refiner. SDXL 1.0 is often used this way, but I've seen people use Z-Image-Turbo for the base model, and Z-Image for the refiner. 

So you would pass the latent to the refiner model. The latent passed to the refiner might be partially de-noised, or fully de-noised, depending on the compatibility of the two models. That would require extra functionality and parameters. 

For instance, denoising_start and denoising_end parameters. A value of denoising_end of 0.8 for the base model, and denoising_start of 0.8 for the refiner model means that it's a seamless handover between the two models at the 80% mark.

Or if two models are not totally compatible with each other (but are still in the same latent-space family), you would pass a clean latent to the refiner model, and then with a parameter called, say, strength, with a value of 0.2, then the refiner effectively jumps to the 80% mark (i.e. goes back 20%). In other words, it adds noise to your latent up to that 80% level, and then starts the denoising process as if it was 80% of the way through already.

Probably an API feature only, I don't think this would work on the command-line.

title: LoRA `_split_qkv_mlp_down` splits shared down-projection and corrupts LoRA weights
author: danielkhalilov
body:
### Bug

In `models/common/lora/mapping/lora_transforms.py`, `_split_qkv_mlp_down` attempts to split a LoRA down-projection tensor when:

```python
rank % num_splits == 0
```

However, for fused QKV / MLP LoRA weights, the down weight is the shared low-rank input projection. Only the up weight should be split by output dimension.

Splitting the down weight corrupts the LoRA decomposition and can produce incorrect generation results.

This condition is true for common LoRA ranks such as 4, 8, 16, and 32, so the corruption can happen silently for many LoRA configurations.

### Current code

```python
@staticmethod
def _split_qkv_mlp_down(tensor: mx.array, index: int, num_splits: int = 4) -> mx.array:
    rank = tensor.shape[0]
    if rank % num_splits == 0:
        chunk_size = rank // num_splits
        start = index * chunk_size
        end = start + chunk_size
        return tensor[start:end, :]
    else:
        return tensor
```

### Why this is wrong

For a fused QKV / MLP LoRA, the up projection is split across the fused output dimensions. The down projection is shared and should remain intact.

Splitting the down projection changes the effective LoRA rank and breaks the decomposition.

### Suggested fix

Return the down weight unchanged:

```python
@staticmethod
def _split_qkv_mlp_down(tensor: mx.array, index: int, num_splits: int = 4) -> mx.array:
    return tensor
```

### Environment

* mflux installed as a vMLX dependency
* Affects fused QKV / MLP LoRA weights where rank is divisible by `num_splits`
* Common ranks affected: 4, 8, 16, 32

title: Option to suppress or reduce EXIF metadata writing
author: plz12345
body:
At present, mflux silently writes a bunch of EXIF data to every image.  While this can be good in that it helps others identify AI-gen images, it can also be bad in that it exposes prompts, settings, LoRAs used, etc., which potentially risks the originator's unique inputs being stolen/reused.

mflux always embeds metadata into every generated image regardless of flags. Here's what's included:

```
EXIF UserComment (always, all formats) — full JSON blob with:

mflux_version, model, base_model
seed, steps, guidance (null if model doesn't support it)
height, width, precision, quantize
generation_time_seconds, created_at (ISO timestamp)
prompt, negative_prompt
lora_paths, lora_scales
image_path / image_paths, image_strength (img2img / edit)
controlnet_image_path, controlnet_strength
masked_image_path, depth_image_path
redux_image_paths, redux_image_strengths
If built from another mflux image: carries original fields with original_ prefix
```

This essentially makes every image it produces 100% reliably, identically reproducible by a 3rd party.

I'm opening this issue to gauge interest and support for making this be optional, but leaving on by default.  I understand there are plenty of methods to bypass this risk, but it's extra work for an artist to have to go through to protect their work.  As a middle ground, I'd support leaving just the generic stuff like mflux version and model version, but dropping the rest.

title: LoRA loader splits the shared rank/down dimension for fused qkv layers → matmul shape error loading kohya/BFL FLUX LoRAs with rank divisible by the split count (e.g. rank 64)
author: deadmansahil
body:
## Summary

`LoraTransforms._split_qkv_mlp_down` (and `_split_qkv_down`) split the **rank/down** dimension of a fused qkv LoRA when the rank is divisible by the number of splits. The down projection of a fused qkv layer is **shared** across q/k/v(/mlp) and is rank-dimensioned, so it must be returned whole — only the **up** projection should be sliced (along its output dimension). Because it is sliced, the resulting per-component `down` has a smaller rank than its matching `up`, and the first denoise step fails with a matmul shape mismatch.

This breaks loading of essentially every kohya / sd-scripts (BFL-format) FLUX LoRA whose rank is divisible by 4 — i.e. ranks 64, 32, 16 — that touches the single-block `linear1` (fused qkv+mlp). Many popular community FLUX.1-dev LoRAs are exactly this format (rank 64, alpha 32).

## Environment

- mflux 0.18.0 (also reproduces on current `main`; the relevant code is byte-identical)
- Apple Silicon (M-series), macOS
- Base model: `FLUX.1-dev`, 8-bit quantized

## Reproduction

Any kohya/BFL-format FLUX.1-dev LoRA with rank 64 triggers it, e.g. [`strangerzonehf/Flux-Super-Realism-LoRA`](https://huggingface.co/strangerzonehf/Flux-Super-Realism-LoRA) (also `strangerzonehf/Flux-Midjourney-Mix2-LoRA`, `prithivMLmods/Flux-Long-Toon-LoRA`, etc.):

```bash
# download the LoRA, then:
mflux-generate \
  --base-model dev -q 8 --steps 4 --guidance 3.5 \
  --prompt "a photorealistic portrait" \
  --lora-paths ./super-realism.safetensors --lora-scales 1.0 \
  --output ./out.png
```

The LoRA keys map and apply, but generation fails at the first denoise step:

```
ValueError: [matmul] Last dimension of first input with shape (1,4608,16)
must match second to last dimension of second input with shape (64,3072)
```

(`4608` = 512 text + 4096 image tokens; `16` = 64 / 4 — the rank wrongly divided by the 4-way split.)

LoRAs in diffusers/PEFT format (pre-split, e.g. `Shakker-Labs/FLUX.1-dev-LoRA-add-details`) load fine because they never hit this transform.

## Root cause

In `src/mflux/models/common/lora/mapping/lora_transforms.py`:

```python
@staticmethod
def _split_qkv_mlp_down(tensor: mx.array, index: int, num_splits: int = 4) -> mx.array:
    rank = tensor.shape[0]
    if rank % num_splits == 0:          # <-- triggers for rank 64/32/16
        chunk_size = rank // num_splits
        start = index * chunk_size
        end = start + chunk_size
        return tensor[start:end, :]      # <-- slices the SHARED rank dim
    else:
        return tensor
```

For a fused qkv layer the LoRA stores one shared `down` of shape `(rank, in_features)` and one `up` of shape `(fused_out, rank)`. Splitting the fused layer into q/k/v(/mlp) must slice only `up` along its **output** dimension (which `_split_qkv_mlp_up` / `_split_qkv_up` already do correctly via the `dims` list); the `down` is shared and must be returned at full rank for every component.

`_split_qkv_down` (the double-block path, `num_splits=3`) has the same defect; it only escapes today because common ranks (64/32/16) aren't divisible by 3. A rank like 48 or 96 would break it too.

## Proposed fix

Make both `_split_qkv_down` and `_split_qkv_mlp_down` return the down tensor unchanged (never split the rank dimension):

```python
@staticmethod
def _split_qkv_down(tensor: mx.array, index: int, num_splits: int = 3) -> mx.array:
    # Fused qkv LoRA shares a single rank-dimensioned down projection; return it
    # whole for every q/k/v component (only the up projection is output-split).
    return tensor

@staticmethod
def _split_qkv_mlp_down(tensor: mx.array, index: int, num_splits: int = 4) -> mx.array:
    return tensor
```

This matches the already-correct `else: return tensor` branch (the non-divisible case that works today) and makes it the behavior for all ranks. I have this fix plus a unit test ready and can open a PR.

## Verification

With the fix, `strangerzonehf/Flux-Super-Realism-LoRA` and `Flux-Midjourney-Mix2-LoRA` load (`1254/1254 keys matched, applied to 494 layers`) and render cleanly on FLUX.1-dev 8-bit. Confirmed for ranks 16/32/64.

*(Found while running mflux on Apple Silicon at RBDS AI Lab.)*

title: Golden image comparator: atol is hardcoded to 0, so dark regions stay strict across hardware (low priority)
author: fxd0h
body:
Low priority, more of an observation than a bug. The image tests pass fine on the reference hardware; this only shows up when regenerating references on a different machine, and there is an easy workaround.

## What I noticed

The "close enough" comparator added in #263 (`src/mflux/utils/image_compare.py`) hardcodes `atol=0`:

```python
closeness_array = np.isclose(
    image1_data,
    image2_data,
    rtol=float(os.environ.get("MFLUX_IMAGE_ALLCLOSE_RTOL", 0.1)),
    atol=0,  # ignore absolute tolerance
)
```

`np.isclose` tests `|a - b| <= atol + rtol*|b|`. With `atol=0` that collapses to `|a - b| <= rtol*|b|`, so the tolerance scales with the reference pixel value. Bright pixels get generous slack (a reference value of 200 tolerates about ±20 at rtol=0.1), while near-black pixels get almost none: reference 0 tolerates 0 (exact match required), reference 2 tolerates 0.2 (still an exact match on uint8).

So for dark regions the comparator is effectively back to exact-match, which is the strictness #263 set out to relax. When the same seed runs on different Apple Silicon or a different mlx build, the output is perceptually identical but shadow detail can differ by a level or two, and those small absolute differences on near-black pixels are counted as mismatches. On images with large dark areas that can push the mismatch ratio over the threshold even though the image is clearly correct. This is the same cross-hardware / cross-version fragility behind #93 and #130.

The asymmetry is that `rtol` and the mismatch threshold are both env-overridable (`MFLUX_IMAGE_ALLCLOSE_RTOL`, `MFLUX_IMAGE_MISMATCH_THRESHOLD`), but `atol` is hardcoded, so there is no knob for the one axis dark regions actually need.

## Suggestion

Either of these is enough, and both are tiny:

1. Give `atol` a small default (a couple of levels on the 0..255 scale) so near-black pixels tolerate minor variation.
2. Mirror the existing rtol env var with an `MFLUX_IMAGE_ALLCLOSE_ATOL` and keep the default at 0.

Happy to send a PR if it is useful.

## Environment

M5 Max, mlx 0.31.0. The ideogram and flux2 golden tests fail here on shadow detail while the generated images are visually correct. The same tests also diverge on stock upstream `main` on this machine, so this reads as hardware numeric drift rather than a code regression. The current workaround (raising `MFLUX_IMAGE_ALLCLOSE_RTOL` or `MFLUX_IMAGE_MISMATCH_THRESHOLD`) helps for bright content but does not address the dark-region case, which is why I am flagging `atol` specifically.

title: FIBO (base briaai/FIBO) txt2img produces pure noise — transformer velocity ~5–8× too small
author: gethyper
body:
## Summary

`mflux-generate-fibo` (base FIBO, `briaai/FIBO`) produces **pure rainbow-confetti noise** for every prompt — the final latent never leaves its initial noise. This reproduces via the stock CLI with **no custom code**, at both q8 and full precision, and at both `guidance=4.0` and `guidance=1.0`. I've isolated it to the **transformer's velocity prediction** (VAE, latent packing, weight-loading and scheduler are all fine), and I'm sharing the diagnostics below in the hope it saves someone time.

## Environment

- mflux `0.18.0`, installed from git `main` (`97ac5e62`)
- mlx `0.31.2`
- macOS / Apple Silicon (M-series)
- Model: `briaai/FIBO` (access-granted, weights ~17 GB downloaded fine)

## Reproduction

```bash
mflux-generate-fibo --prompt '{"caption":"a red cube on a white table"}' --steps 50 --seed 42
# also: -q 8, and guidance 1.0 -> identical confetti
```

Output is smooth multicolored blobs with no semantic structure (same for `--steps 8`).

## What is NOT the cause (verified)

- **VAE** — an `encode → decode` round-trip of a real image is near-perfect (e.g. a photo with mean/std 249.9/35.6 comes back 249.9/34.6). De-normalization (`latents*std + mean`) and patchify/unpatchify are correct.
- **Latent packing** — `FiboLatentCreator.pack_latents` / `unpack_latents` are exact inverses (transpose+reshape).
- **Weight loading** — all transformer params load with real trained statistics (`x_embedder.weight` std ≈ 0.083, `context_embedder` 0.009, `proj_out` 0.023, `norm_out.linear` 0.040), i.e. not left at default init.
- **Quantization** — full-precision run (peak ~37 GB) is identical to `-q 8`.
- **CFG** — same at `guidance=4.0` and `guidance=1.0`.
- **Timestep conditioning** — sweeping the value fed to `BriaFiboTimestepProjEmbeddings` (`sigma`, `sigma*1000`, `(1-sigma)*1000`, `1000`) barely moves the result.

## Root cause — transformer velocity is far too small / poorly directed

Diagnostic: encode a real image → `x0` (packed), sample noise `n`, form `x_t = (1-σ)·x0 + σ·n`, run `transformer(...)` and compare the predicted velocity `v` to the rectified-flow target `n - x0`:

| σ | expected | measured |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 (pure noise, t=0) | `std(v) ≈ 1.0` | `std(v) ≈ 0.19` |
| 0.5 | `cos(v, n−x0) ≈ 0.7+`, `std(v) ≈ O(1)` | `cos ≈ 0.2–0.37`, `std(v) ≈ 0.15` vs `std(n−x0) ≈ 1.46` (~8× too small) |

Because `v` is ~5–8× too small (and only weakly correlated with the true direction), the Euler step `latents += (σ_{t+1}−σ_t)·v` barely moves the latent, so after all 50 steps it is still essentially the initial noise → confetti. The magnitude deficit is **invariant to the timestep value**, which rules out the AdaLayerNorm-gate/timestep-embedding hypothesis. All transformer blocks (joint + single) have correct residual connections.

So the discrepancy appears to be somewhere in the transformer forward — candidates I haven't yet pinned down: the RoPE image/text position ids, the per-block SmolLM3 `text_encoder_layers` injection (`encoder_hidden_states[:, :, :1536]` concatenated with `caption_projection(layer_i)`), or an attention scale — i.e. something that corrupts the predicted direction/magnitude without touching the VAE or scheduler.

## Possibly-related minor inconsistency

`variants/txt2img/fibo.py` never applies a sigma shift, whereas `variants/edit/fibo_edit.py` does (it calls `config.scheduler.set_mu(FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler._compute_linear_mu(config.image_seq_len))`). Both configs have `requires_sigma_shift=False`, so the generic `Config.scheduler` path skips `set_image_seq_len` for txt2img. Adding the `set_mu` call to `fibo.py` changes the schedule but does **not** fix the confetti — noting it only in case it's a real oversight.

## Ask

Could a maintainer confirm the intended FIBO txt2img flow (timestep convention + whether txt2img should also apply the sigma shift), and whether the per-block `text_encoder_layers` injection / RoPE ids match the reference `BriaFiboTransformer2DModel`? Happy to run further numerical probes or test a patch — I have the model loaded and the diagnostic scripts ready.

title: Perf: `_hist_match` inverts a permutation via a second `np.argsort` (O(N log N) → O(N))
author: bobmatnyc
body:
### Summary

`SeedVR2Util._hist_match` inverts a permutation by running a **second full `np.argsort`**, which is O(N log N) where an O(N) scatter is exact and sufficient. On the full 2×-upscaled image (tens of millions of pixels), and called 3× per upscale (L/a/b channels), this line noticeably dominated runtime in our downstream use.

### Location

`mflux/models/seedvr2/variants/upscale/seedvr2_util.py`, `_hist_match` (lines ~231–234 in v0.18.0):

```python
src_idx = np.argsort(src, kind="stable")   # forward sort
ref_sorted = np.sort(ref, kind="stable")
inv = np.argsort(src_idx, kind="stable")   # <-- inverts the permutation via ANOTHER O(N log N) sort
out[i] = ref_sorted[inv].reshape(source.shape[1:]).astype(np.float32)
```

`inv = np.argsort(src_idx, ...)` computes the inverse of the permutation `src_idx`. Since `src_idx` is a permutation of `range(N)` (unique indices, no ties), its inverse can be built directly with an O(N) scatter — no comparison sort needed.

### Why it's slow

- `apply_color_correction` → `_lab_color_transfer_exact` calls `_hist_match` 3× (L, a, b channels) per SeedVR2 upscale.
- It runs on the full, already-2×-upscaled image, so N is tens of millions of pixels per channel.
- The inverse is computed by sorting an int64 index array (O(N log N)) instead of scattering (O(N)).

### Measurement

Isolating just the inverse-permutation step on 10M elements:

- Double-`argsort` (current): **~6.6 s**
- O(N) scatter (proposed): **~0.05 s**

≈ **125×** faster on the isolated step. In our application this was the difference between a snappy upscale and multi-minute stalls / apparent hangs on large photos.

### Proposed fix (drop-in, output-identical)

```python
inv = np.empty_like(src_idx)
inv[src_idx] = np.arrange(src_idx.size, dtype=src_idx.dtype)
```

This produces the exact inverse permutation (indices are unique, no ties), so the output is mathematically identical — only the complexity changes from O(N log N) to O(N).

Optional secondary note: the two forward `kind="stable"` sorts (`np.argsort(src, ...)` / `np.sort(ref, ...)`) could use the default (quicksort) since histogram matching on continuous pixel values doesn't require a stable tie-break — a smaller additional win. The inverse-permutation change above is the main one.

### Version affected

mflux `0.18.0` (installed from PyPI). Happy to open a PR if that's helpful.

title: Qwen-Image 4-bit: quantization noise compounds per denoising step (flat-field σ grows monotonically with steps)
author: SteveGJones
body:
## Summary

Running a 4-bit quantized Qwen-Image export on mflux 0.18.0, background grain/mottling gets **worse as step count increases**, not better. A flat-field diagnostic shows high-frequency noise growing monotonically with steps, which points to per-step accumulation of quantization error rather than a fixed noise floor.

## Environment

- mflux **0.18.0** (uv tool install), Apple M2 Max, 32 GB, macOS (Darwin 25.5)
- Model: `OsaurusAI/Qwen-Image-mflux-4bit` (saved with mflux 0.18, so not the pre-0.13 vintage problem from #296)

## Repro

Render a flat field — a prompt asking for a single solid white color block fill — and measure high-frequency noise as `σ = std(image − gaussian_blur(image, 4))` over a 512² crop:

```bash
mflux-generate-qwen --model OsaurusAI/Qwen-Image-mflux-4bit \
  --prompt "A plain solid pure white image. Uniform white color fill, nothing else." \
  --seed 42 --width 512 --height 512 --steps <N>
```

| Steps | hf σ | Mean (target 255) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 2.48 | ~252 |
| 8 | 4.14 | — |
| 20 | 6.42 | — |
| 50 | 7.36 | ~224 |

Both trends move the wrong way with more steps: noise grows ~3×, and the white point drifts 252 → 224. The same instrument on other 4-bit families on the same machine/runtime reads an order of magnitude lower and step-stable (FLUX.2-klein-4B 4-bit: σ 0.33; Z-Image-Turbo 4-bit: σ 0.44) — so this looks specific to how the Qwen path interacts with uniform 4-bit quantization, not a general runtime issue.

Things we ruled out: guidance (tested at 4.0), native resolution (1664×928), prompt phrasing/negative prompts — none change the grain. The RGB single-color variants of the flat-field test show the same behavior.

## Hypothesis / possible fix vector

Uniform q4 across all layers + iterative denoising means per-step weight error compounds across the trajectory (a single-pass q4 LLM never accumulates this way). The mixed-precision quantization work in #420 (protecting sensitive layers from q4) seems like the natural fix vector — Qwen-Image may be an especially strong motivating case for it, since its practical step optimum on 4-bit collapses to ~8 steps (above that, added steps degrade the image).

Happy to run further diagnostics on this hardware if useful.
