title: Golden image tests are brittle on dark references (ImageCompare uses atol=0)
author: plz12345
body:
## Symptom

`tests/image_generation/test_generate_image_ideogram4_golden.py::TestImageGeneratorIdeogram4Golden::test_ideogram4_jazz_fest_json_caption` fails locally on `main`:

```
AssertionError: Generated image doesn't match reference image.
their elements are 28.4% different. Fails assertion for mismatch_threshold=0.15
```

The generated image is visually correct — same composition, typography, and trumpet-player pose as the reference, differing only in slight hue/contrast.

Found while running the slow suite for #444; that PR is not the cause (see below).

## Root cause

`ImageCompare.check_images_close_enough` (`src/mflux/utils/image_compare.py`) compares with:

```python
np.isclose(image1_data, image2_data, rtol=0.1, atol=0)  # atol=0, "ignore absolute tolerance"
```

`atol=0` makes the tolerance purely *relative*, so it collapses to nothing on dark pixels: a reference pixel of 3 tolerates only ±0.3, so any 1/255 difference fails. A reference pixel of 0 tolerates nothing at all.

The jazz-fest poster is a near-black design. Measured on the actual image pair:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| mean abs diff | 3.92 / 255 (1.5%) |
| median abs diff | 1 / 255 |
| p95 abs diff | 10 / 255 |
| reference elements that are dark (<32) | **90.7%** |
| mismatches occurring in dark pixels | **89.1%** |

So very small numeric differences are amplified into a 28.4% "mismatch" purely because the image is dark. The comparator is the amplifier, not the image generation.

Mismatch ratio as a function of `atol` on the same pair (`rtol=0.1` throughout):

| atol | mismatch | vs 0.15 threshold |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (current) | 28.4% | ❌ fail |
| 1 | 16.6% | ❌ fail |
| 2 | 11.6% | ✅ pass |
| 4 | 7.1% | ✅ pass |
| 8 | 4.3% | ✅ pass |

## What it is not

- **Not mlx version drift.** The `[dev]` pin was `mlx==0.31.0` when the reference was committed (0a1b0fe, "Add Ideogram 4 FP8 support" #433) and is still `mlx==0.31.0` on `main`.
- **Not the mlx ≤0.31.2 quantized-matmul issue.** That affects quantized matmuls above 32768 rows; this test runs `quantize=None` at 768×576.
- **Not flakiness.** Two independent runs on the same machine produced pixel-identical output (`np.array_equal` → `True`, max abs diff `0`). It is deterministic per machine.
- **Not #444.** The same 28.4% occurs on `main`, and the outputs from both branches are pixel-identical. The golden path never constructs `StepwiseHandler`.

The residual difference is consistent with ordinary cross-machine floating-point variation: the reference was generated on the original contributor's hardware, and this run was on an Apple M5 Pro / macOS 26.5.2.

Worth noting that no golden test currently runs in CI — the Actions workflow runs `-m fast` only, so these can only fail locally.

## Suggested fix

1. **Give `ImageCompare` a small `atol`.** `atol=2` puts this test at 11.6%, comfortably under threshold, while preserving the existing `rtol` behaviour in bright regions. This addresses the whole class of dark-reference golden tests rather than this one case. The current `atol=0` carries an explicit "ignore absolute tolerance" comment, so it looks deliberate — happy to hear if there was a specific reason for it.
2. **Regenerate the reference PNG.** Cheaper, but pins the reference to whichever machine regenerates it and is likely to re-break on different hardware. If done, best done after (1) so the new reference is validated under a comparator that isn't scale-free.
3. Raising `mismatch_threshold` for this test would mask it — the value would have to exceed 0.284 with no principled basis.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run python -m pytest -k ideogram -m slow -v
```

Requires `ideogram-ai/ideogram-4-fp8` (27.55 GB). Note that the slow run overwrites `tests/resources/output_ideogram4_jazz_fest.png` in the working tree, since `MFLUX_PRESERVE_TEST_OUTPUT=1` is set by `make test`.

## Open question

Only the two ideogram slow tests were run here. It would be worth a full `make test-slow` sweep to see whether other dark-reference golden tests show the same pattern — that would confirm whether this is a general comparator issue or specific to this reference.

**Partially answered in the follow-up comment below:** a darkness survey of all committed references shows `reference_ideogram4_jazz_fest.png` is a large outlier at 90.7% dark (next-darkest 48.3%), and a passing control (`test_seedvr2_7b_upscale`) has 100% of its residual mismatches in dark pixels despite those being only 23.5% of the image. A full sweep is still outstanding.

title: --metadata writes literal `null` for FLUX.2 CLIs (sidecar JSON has no params)
author: TresPies-source
body:
### Summary

`--metadata` writes the literal `null` instead of generation parameters for the
FLUX.2 CLIs. Every other model family writes a correct sidecar. The result is a
4-byte `.metadata.json` file, so FLUX.2 renders carry no reproducibility record.

### Reproduction

```bash
mflux-generate-flux2 --prompt "a red cube" --quantize 8 \
  --height 512 --width 512 --steps 4 --seed 7 \
  --metadata --output out.png

cat out.metadata.json   # -> null
```

Compare with a model that works:

```bash
mflux-generate-z-image-turbo --prompt "a red cube" --quantize 8 \
  --height 512 --width 512 --steps 8 --seed 7 \
  --metadata --output out2.png

cat out2.metadata.json   # -> full params (model, seed, steps, quantize, prompt, ...)
```

**Expected:** the same sidecar contents as every other model family.
**Actual:** the 4-byte literal `null`.

### Root cause

`Flux2Klein.generate_image()` returns a `GeneratedImage`, which carries its
`Config` and knows how to serialize it via `GeneratedImage.save()` →
`ImageUtil.save_image(..., self._get_metadata(), ...)`.

The FLUX.2 CLIs bypass that and call the **static** helper directly, without
passing `metadata`:

```python
# mflux/models/flux2/cli/flux2_generate.py:68
ImageUtil.save_image(
    image=image,
    path=args.output.format(seed=seed),
    export_json_metadata=args.metadata,
)
```

`ImageUtil.save_image` declares `metadata: dict | None = None`
(`mflux/utils/image_util.py:229`), so `metadata` stays `None` and
`json.dump(None, json_file)` writes `null`.

Other CLIs do not hit this because they call the instance method — e.g.
`mflux/models/z_image/cli/z_image_turbo_generate.py`:

```python
image.save(path=args.output.format(seed=seed), export_json_metadata=args.metadata)
```

### Scope

Only the two call sites that use the static helper from a CLI:

- `mflux/models/flux2/cli/flux2_generate.py:68`
- `mflux/models/flux2/cli/flux2_edit_generate.py:76`

### Proposed fix

Use the instance method, matching the other CLIs:

```python
image.save(
    path=args.output.format(seed=seed),
    export_json_metadata=args.metadata,
)
```

Verified locally on `flux2_generate.py`: the sidecar goes from 4 bytes (`null`)
to 719 bytes of correct parameters (model `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B`,
seed 7, steps 4, quantize 8, prompt, timings). I applied the identical change to
`flux2_edit_generate.py` because it is the same pattern, but I did **not**
exercise the edit path at runtime — that one is unverified.

Happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

### Environment

- mflux 0.18.0 (PyPI), Python 3.12.13
- macOS 26.5.2, Apple M1 Pro, 32 GB
- mlx 0.32.0
- Model: `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B`

### Unrelated observation

While reducing the repro I hit a separate `ZeroDivisionError: float division by
zero` from `mflux-generate-flux2 --steps 1`. Not filing it here since it is a
distinct issue — happy to open a second one if it is not already known.

title: --steps 1 raises ZeroDivisionError in shared FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler (not a one-line guard)
author: TresPies-source
body:
### Summary

`--steps 1` raises `ZeroDivisionError` in `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler`.
This is in the **shared** scheduler (`mflux/models/common/schedulers/`), not in
any one model's code, so it affects every model family that selects
`flow_match_euler_discrete`.

It is **not** a one-line guard — the obvious fix moves the failure one layer
down. Details below, since that seemed worth saving you the round trip.

### Reproduction

```bash
mflux-generate-flux2 --prompt "x" --quantize 8 \
  --height 512 --width 512 --steps 1 --seed 7 --output out.png
```

```
File "mflux/models/common/schedulers/flow_match_euler_discrete_scheduler.py", line 110,
      in _compute_timesteps_and_sigmas
    - i * (sigma_max - sigma_min) * self.num_train_timesteps / (num_steps - 1)
ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
```

Reproducible with no model or weights at all:

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from mflux.models.common.schedulers.flow_match_euler_discrete_scheduler import (
    FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler as S,
)

for n in (1, 2, 4):
    cfg = SimpleNamespace(num_inference_steps=n, model_config=SimpleNamespace())
    S(cfg)   # n=1 -> ZeroDivisionError; n=2 and n=4 fine
```

### Layer 1

`_compute_timesteps_and_sigmas()` spreads `i` over `num_steps - 1`, which is 0
when `num_steps == 1`.

### Layer 2 — why the obvious guard is not enough

Changing the denominator to `max(num_steps - 1, 1)` gets past line 110 and then
fails in `_stretch_to_terminal()`:

```
File ".../flow_match_euler_discrete_scheduler.py", line 101, in _stretch_to_terminal
    stretched = [1.0 - (oms / scale_factor) for oms in one_minus_sigmas]
ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero
```

The `n == 1` schedule degenerates:

```
timesteps_linear = [1000.0]        # only i=0 exists
sigmas_linear    = [1.0]
sigmas_shifted   = [1.0]           # exp(1)/(exp(1) + (1/1 - 1)^1) = 1.0
one_minus_sigmas = [0.0]
scale_factor     = 0.0 / (1.0 - shift_terminal) = 0.0   # then divided by
```

So with a single step there is no terminal to stretch toward — `shift_terminal`
has nothing to act on. That is a semantics question about what a 1-step
flow-match schedule *should* be, which is why I am not proposing a patch.

### A reference point

The sibling static method in the same class, `get_timesteps_and_sigmas()` (used
by `set_image_seq_len`), handles `n == 1` without trouble:

```python
sigmas = mx.linspace(1.0, 1.0 / num_inference_steps, num_inference_steps, dtype=mx.float32)
```

`mx.linspace(1.0, 1.0, 1)` → `[1.0]`, and that path never calls
`_stretch_to_terminal`. If the two paths are meant to agree, that difference may
be the more interesting bug.

### Scope

- `flow_match_euler_discrete_scheduler.py:110` is the **only** `(num_steps - 1)`
  division among the four schedulers in `models/common/schedulers/`.
  `linear_scheduler.py` and `seedvr2_euler_scheduler.py` do not have it — which
  is why `mflux-generate-z-image-turbo --steps 1` is unaffected (turbo selects
  `linear`).
- By grep, the affected scheduler is selected by:
  - **flux2** — klein txt2img, edit, training adapter
  - **fibo** — txt2img, edit
  - **z_image** — its guidance-supporting path
- Verification honesty: I reproduced this at runtime only through
  `mflux-generate-flux2`, plus the standalone snippet above.
  I did not download fibo or non-turbo z-image, so treat those two as
  static analysis rather than confirmed.

### Impact

Low severity — `--steps 2` works and 1 step is not a useful quality setting.
Filing because the failure is a bare `ZeroDivisionError` from library internals
rather than a validation message, so it reads as a crash rather than "that value
is out of range." A parser-level minimum for schedulers that need ≥2 steps would
also be a reasonable resolution.

### Environment

- mflux 0.18.0 (PyPI), Python 3.12.13, mlx 0.32.0
- macOS 26.5.2, Apple M1 Pro, 32 GB
- Model: `black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B`

Split out from #493 as suggested there.

title: load_image ignores EXIF orientation, so phone photos are fed to the model sideways
author: markthebest12
body:
**mflux version:** 0.18.0
**Platform:** macOS 26.5 (arm64), MLX 0.31.2

### Summary

`ImageUtil.load_image` opens images without applying EXIF orientation, so any JPEG carrying a
non-1 `Orientation` tag — which is most photos straight off a phone — reaches the model rotated.
The image is not merely saved with the wrong orientation; it is *conditioned on* sideways, so
edit models produce wrong output rather than correctly-oriented output that needs a flip.

### Where

`mflux/utils/image_util.py`:

```python
@staticmethod
def load_image(image_or_path):
    ...
    return PIL.Image.open(image_or_path).convert("RGB")
```

There is no `ImageOps.exif_transpose` call here, and `grep -rn exif_transpose` returns nothing
anywhere in the installed package.

### Why it matters more than it looks

Two things make this worse than a cosmetic orientation bug:

1. **It is silently format-dependent.** HEIC inputs are unaffected, because `pillow-heif`
   normalises orientation during decode. So the *same photograph* exported as HEIC and as JPEG
   produces materially different renders through the same code path, with nothing in the logs
   indicating why.

2. **Edit models try to compensate.** In a 21-render comparison we ran across three models, the
   single EXIF-rotated input (a 4032×3024 iPhone JPEG, `Orientation=6`) was fed sideways to 6
   renders. FLUX.2-klein absorbed the rotation and edited faithfully. Qwen-Image-Edit-2509
   instead attempted to "correct" the orientation mid-edit and produced the two worst artifacts
   in the entire matrix. A user hitting this sees a bad *edit*, not a rotated one, which points
   debugging in the wrong direction.

### Reproduction

```python
from mflux.utils.image_util import ImageUtil
# any JPEG with EXIF Orientation=6 (portrait photo from an iPhone)
img = ImageUtil.load_image("IMG_0001.jpg")
print(img.size)   # (4032, 3024) -- landscape, though the photo is portrait
```

Compare against `PIL.ImageOps.exif_transpose(PIL.Image.open("IMG_0001.jpg"))`, which yields
`(3024, 4032)`.

### Suggested fix

```python
from PIL import ImageOps

return ImageOps.exif_transpose(PIL.Image.open(image_or_path)).convert("RGB")
```

`exif_transpose` is a no-op for images with no orientation tag or `Orientation=1`, so this is
safe for every input that works correctly today. Applying it before `.convert("RGB")` keeps the
EXIF block readable at the point of the call.

Happy to open a PR if you'd like it in that form.

title: --negative-prompt is accepted and silently discarded on FLUX.1, and inconsistently handled elsewhere
author: fxd0h
body:
The shared parser exposes `--negative-prompt` on every image CLI (`parsers.py:118`). What happens to it after that depends on the family. Checked against current main:

**FLUX.1: dead parameter.** `flux_generate.py:66` reads the flag and passes it into `Flux.generate_image`; the name appears exactly twice in the whole `src/mflux/models/flux/` tree, that call and the signature that receives it (`flux.py:59`). The value is read from the user, plumbed through one call, and dropped, on dev and schnell, with nothing said. If there is a consumer I did not find I am happy to be corrected, but a grep of the family tree comes back with only those two hits.

**Ideogram 4: no parameter at all.** There is no `negative_prompt` anywhere under `src/mflux/models/ideogram4/`, while the CLI still accepts the flag. This family already warns for `--steps` and `--guidance` (`ideogram4_generate.py:44-46`), so the idiom exists, just not for this flag.

**Z-Image and the guidance-distilled models: dropped for a correct reason, silently.** `z_image.py:60-61` pins guidance to 0.0 when `supports_guidance` is false, and the encode path skips the negative encoding at guidance <= 1.0. The math is right, CFG needs guidance above 1. But it is silent, including when the user passed an explicit `--guidance` that then got overridden. And on base Z-Image an omitted `--guidance` defaults to 0.0, so the everyday invocation with a negative prompt and no guidance flag ignores the negative prompt without a word.

Why this matters beyond tidiness: downstream tools transcribe capability lists from `--help`, and `--help` currently says every model takes a negative prompt. We hit this through a tool that had been declaring `--negative-prompt` support on models that discard it, including in its defaults.

We shipped one policy for this in mflux-cv (HowDidTheCatGetSoFat/mflux-cv#39): keep accepting the options so existing scripts do not break, and warn in Ideogram's existing message format whenever a provided option will be dropped, keyed on the effective post-resolution behavior rather than the flag value. Happy to port that here if warn-everywhere is the direction you want. Erroring instead, or removing the dead FLUX.1 parameter, are the other options; that call is yours.

title: RuntimeError: 'There is no Stream(gpu, N) in current thread' when calling generate_image from non-main thread
author: dahai80
body:
## Bug Report

**Scenario — generate_image crashes in thread executor**

1. A caller runs `model.generate_image(...)` inside a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` (e.g., a web server like ComfyUI handling requests on worker threads).
2. Inside the denoising loop, `mx.eval(latents)` triggers GPU computation.
3. MLX raises `RuntimeError: There is no Stream(gpu, 4) in current thread` because the worker thread has no GPU stream.

**Root Cause**: MLX uses thread-local GPU streams. The default stream is only created on the main thread. When `mx.eval()` runs on a non-main thread, no stream exists for that thread, causing the crash. mflux has 39 `mx.eval()` calls across 32 files and zero thread-safety / stream management code.

**Reproduction** (requires Apple Silicon + MLX):
```python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from mflux import Flux1

model = Flux1.from_name("flux-schnell")

def gen():
    return model.generate_image(seed=42, prompt="a cat", num_inference_steps=4)

# This works:
gen()

# This crashes with RuntimeError:
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as ex:
    ex.submit(gen).result()
```

**Error**:
```
RuntimeError: There is no Stream(gpu, 4) in current thread
```

**Fix**: Add a thread-local GPU stream context manager that each `generate_image()` method wraps its body in. MLX provides `mx.new_thread_local_stream(mx.gpu)` and `mx.stream()` for exactly this purpose. When running on the main thread, the context manager is a no-op (the default stream already exists). When running on a worker thread, it creates the missing stream.

This is especially important for downstream integrations (ComfyUI, web APIs, async servers) that need to run generation on worker threads.

**Affected files** (all 21 `generate_image` methods + initializers with `mx.eval`):
- `src/mflux/models/flux/variants/*/flux*.py` (10 files)
- `src/mflux/models/flux2/variants/*/flux2_*.py` (2 files)
- `src/mflux/models/krea2/variants/txt2img/krea2.py`
- `src/mflux/models/ideogram4/variants/txt2img/ideogram4.py`
- `src/mflux/models/qwen/variants/*/qwen_image*.py` (2 files)
- `src/mflux/models/fibo/variants/*/fibo*.py` (2 files)
- `src/mflux/models/z_image/variants/z_image.py`
- `src/mflux/models/ernie_image/variants/txt2img/ernie_image.py`
- `src/mflux/models/seedvr2/variants/upscale/seedvr2.py`
- `src/mflux/models/krea2/krea2_initializer.py`
- `src/mflux/models/ideogram4/ideogram4_initializer.py`
- `src/mflux/models/ernie_image/ernie_image_initializer.py`

title: Support explicit false overrides for metadata-restored boolean CLI flags
author: coderabbitai[bot]
body:
## Summary

`CommandLineParser` restores metadata-backed `store_true` flags without a way for the command line to explicitly set those flags to `false`.

This is pre-existing parser behavior. PR #490 exposed it through `pid_decode`, but the issue is parser-wide and must not receive a PiD-only fix.

## Required changes

- Audit every boolean flag that `CommandLineParser` restores from `--config-from-metadata`.
- Change the affected argument definitions to use `argparse.BooleanOptionalAction`, or implement an equivalent tri-state sentinel.
- Preserve the distinction between:
  - flag omitted on the command line;
  - flag explicitly enabled; and
  - flag explicitly disabled.
- Apply metadata values only when the user did not provide either form of the affected CLI flag.
- Keep the command line higher priority than metadata in both directions.
- Update parser tests for all affected metadata-restored boolean flags.

Affected examples today include `pid_decode` and `controlnet_save_canny`. The implementation must sweep all metadata-restored boolean flags rather than enumerate only these examples.

## User-visible behavior

The change adds `--no-<flag>` forms to `--help` for every affected flag. This is user-visible, but it must not change default behavior when metadata is not used.

## Acceptance criteria

For each affected flag:

1. Given `--config-from-metadata <sidecar>` where the metadata value is `true`, parsing without an explicit flag restores `true`.
2. Given the same sidecar, `--no-<flag>` produces `false`.
3. Given metadata where the value is `false`, an explicit positive flag remains `true`.
4. Metadata does not override an explicitly supplied CLI value in either direction.
5. Tests cover omitted, explicitly enabled, and explicitly disabled states.

## Scope exclusion

Do not include the PiD RNG item from the `pid_sampler.py` review thread. That concerns code introduced by PR #490 and belongs in that PR's follow-up list.

## Context

Requested by @plz12345.

- PR that surfaced the behavior: https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/pull/490
- Review discussion: https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/pull/490#discussion_r3755796351

title: CUDA rendering fails on some on MFlux quantised models (fix hinted at)
author: ianscrivener
body:
I'm connected to the internet with 5G so I some processes on cloud GPU (Modal, RunPod, others)

Today was testing FIBO and run into an error. Found the same error on some other models.

**Typical error on CUDA** 
```
RuntimeError: [quantized_matmul] No implementation for problem shape: 2480x4096x128x1 activation: 
bfloat16, bits: 4, group size: 64, mode: "affine". 
```

### TLDR 
**MFlux quantizes every layer, including tiny ones. MLX's Metal kernels handle any matrix shape... but newer CUDA kernels don't cover the small ones. Suggested fix (CUDA only): at load time, find the quantized layers CUDA can't run and dequantize just those back to bf16. No changes to model files.**

Long form discussion: [CUDA Generation fix](https://github.com/orgs/mflux-community/discussions/562)

I wanted to socialize this with everyone else before I even thought about doing any coding. TBH this fix feels like it's above my pay grade.

title: mflux-generate-boogu --metadata writes a null sidecar
author: fxd0h
body:
### Summary

`mflux-generate-boogu --metadata` writes a sidecar containing the literal `null` instead of the generation parameters.

### Cause

The CLI hands the `GeneratedImage` to `ImageUtil.save_image()` as if it were a PIL image:

```python
ImageUtil.save_image(image=image, path=args.output.format(seed=seed), export_json_metadata=args.metadata)
```

`save_image` then calls `image.save(file_path)`, which lands back in `GeneratedImage.save()` and re-enters with its own metadata, so the PNG does keep its embedded xmp/IPTC/exif. The sidecar, though, is written by the outer call, whose `metadata` argument is None, and `json.dump(None)` is the four bytes `null`.

Every other generate CLI calls `image.save(path=..., export_json_metadata=args.metadata)` directly and gets a full sidecar.

### Reproduction

```bash
mflux-generate-boogu --prompt "a red cube" -q 8 --steps 4 --seed 7 --metadata --output out.png
cat out.metadata.json   # -> null
```

Same shape as #493, which #492 fixed for the FLUX.2 CLIs.

title: Release blockers for 0.19.0: correctness fixes from the growth-week audit
author: anthonywu
body:
I am offering to put up PRs to address these in a big sweep, but before I spend the time I want to check if anyone thinks any of these are false-positives.

-----

Tracking issue for the P0 correctness items found in an audit of the 45 PRs merged Aug 10–13 (full audit with evidence available; every item below was verified at `5c0bc14a` by live repro or source inspection). 45 PRs are currently unreleased on main — these should land before tagging **0.19.0**. Process-side hardening (CI lint gate, test selector, branch protection, PR template) is handled separately in #576.

**Root-cause context:** model/config truth is duplicated across 5+ hand-maintained tables (`AVAILABLE_MODELS`, `ui_defaults.MODEL_CHOICES`, `MODEL_INFERENCE_STEPS`, `mflux-save` substring dispatch, `ConfigResolution._create_config`'s field whitelist), so each growth-week PR updated a different subset and aliases now fail somewhere new. Items marked 🧩 below are all one bug with seven symptoms — a single `AVAILABLE_MODELS`-derived registry would close them at once.

### Model registry / config resolution

- [x] **`--model <alias>` crashes for 16 root keys + ~40 aliases** 🧩 — `cli/parser/parsers.py:536-537` vs stale hand-maintained `ui_defaults.MODEL_CHOICES`. Repro: `mflux-generate-lens --model lens-turbo --prompt test` → `FileNotFoundError: Model not found: 'lens-turbo'` (its own canonical alias). Same for `krea-2-raw`, `qwen-image`, all `klein-*`/`boogu-*`/`zimage*`/`fiboedit*`; `--base-model qwen-image` also argparse-rejected. Fix: derive choices from `AVAILABLE_MODELS`; validate `--base-model` via `ConfigResolution`.  Covered by #592 and as a sub-issue #591 
- [x] **Default `--steps` = 25 on 10 CLIs** 🧩 — split out as #580, PR #581. `parsers.py:506-508` reads `namespace.model`, which is `None` when the model fallback lives in `main()` instead of `parser.set_defaults`. Verified: boogu 25 (want 4), krea2 25 (`DEFAULT_STEPS=8` dead code), lens 25 (want 4), z-image-turbo 25 (want 9), flux2/flux2-edit 25 (klein wants 4), z-image 25 (want 50), qwen/qwen-edit 25 (want 20), ideogram4 25 (want 20); `MODEL_INFERENCE_STEPS` also misses the new aliases. Fix as landed: key the steps table by canonical `AVAILABLE_MODELS` key and resolve aliases through the registry + `add_model_arguments(default_model=...)` per CLI. Note `parser.set_defaults(model=...)`, suggested above, would inject a broken `model_path` for lens and qwen-edit via the first checkbox's bug — see #580 for the measurement.
- [x] **`mflux-save` silently misclassifies models** 🧩 — `models/common/cli/save.py:24-46` substring chain with `else: Flux1`. Verified via mocked constructors: `lens/lens-turbo`→Flux1, `klein-4b/9b/9b-kv`→Flux1, `seedvr2*`→Flux1, `z-image-controlnet*`→`ZImage` (wrong variant), `fibo-edit*`→txt2img `FIBO`. No error on unmatched names. Fix: dispatch via `ModelConfig.from_name` + class on the config; `parser.error()` on unmatched. Split out as a sub-issue #606
- [x] **#574 regression + root bug: `ConfigResolution._create_config` drops 9 of 23 `ModelConfig` fields** — `config_resolution.py:127-142`. Repro: `resolve('Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit-2511')` returns sigma 1.15/4096/None (should be 0.9/8192/0.02 → wrong schedule); `--base-model flux2-klein-4b` + custom path loses `text_encoder_overrides` → text encoder built with wrong dims; klein-9b-kv loses `supports_kv_cache`; ernie loses sigma shifts + lora-training defaults. Post-#574, `resolve('qwen-edit-2511')` now yields `model_name=2509` → from_name paths silently serve **2509 weights**. Fix: propagate every field (`dataclasses.replace`-style copy overriding only `model_name`/`base_model`) + a resolution test asserting sigma/TE/kv fields per alias. Consider reverting #574's premise (its stated mechanism was verified backwards).
- [x] **`--model` silently ignored on 4 CLIs; capabilities claims "honored"** — hardcoded configs in `krea2_generate.py:46`, `z_image_turbo_generate.py:37`, `ernie_image_generate.py:37`, `ernie_image_turbo_generate.py:48`. Verified: `krea2 --model dev` still builds `krea/Krea-2-Turbo`, no warning. Fix: declare in `IGNORED_OPTIONS` (so #499 warns) or family-validate like `lens_generate.py:36-41` does; fix the false contract records. Fixed in #614 (family-validate route): all four CLIs plus `lens_generate` now go through `ConfigResolution.resolve_restricted` — a builtin name must be an alias of the CLI's own model, while paths and repo ids (which `parse_args` marks by setting `model_path`) keep the CLI's config and load weights from the path. The capabilities record needed no correction in the end: `--model` is now genuinely honored. Note the same false "honored" status still stands on the upscale CLIs (see @fxd0h's comment below) — separate scope.
- [x] **`mflux-completions` crashes on every build path** — `cli/completions/generator.py:258-259` adds lora args twice for `mflux-upscale-controlnet`. Repro: `mflux-completions --print` → `argparse.ArgumentError: conflicting option string: --lora-style`, exit 1. Fix: delete the duplicated line; lean-followup: enumerate commands from `importlib.metadata.entry_points` like capabilities does (list currently misses 6 CLIs).

### LoRA handling

- [x] **boogu & FIBO accept `--lora` then silently discard it** — `boogu_initializer.py:38-39` hardcodes `lora_paths = []` (no warning, capabilities reports `lora: true`); `fibo_generate.py:44-51` never forwards them and `fibo_initializer.py:20-21` never applies. Parser still resolves/downloads the files — user pays for a no-op. Fix: implement LoRA application, or declare the flags in `REJECTED_OPTIONS` and stop advertising. Split out as a sub-issue #615, fixed in #616. Two additions to the scope above: `mflux-generate-fibo-edit` forwards the LoRA kwargs via `lora_init_kwargs_from_args` and is equally affected, and `mflux-save` filtered the same kwargs away by constructor signature, writing an unmodified checkpoint for `--model boogu --lora ...`. Taken the stop-advertising route, but by removing the flags rather than declaring them in `REJECTED_OPTIONS`: declaring keeps them registered, so `--help`, the completions and the capabilities dump would all still list them, and refusing before the download needs new parser machinery — whereas `mflux-generate-lens` is already the precedent for a LoRA-less model and simply does not register them. Happy to switch if the explicit "not supported for this model" message is worth the surface.
- [x] **LoRA metadata restore merges instead of overriding; breaks cross-machine** — `parsers.py:418-429, 524-532`. Stubbed repro: sidecar `lora_paths:["a"]` + `--lora-paths b` → both apply (`['a','b']`); restored absolute paths re-validated → sidecar from another machine exits `LoRA file not found`. Fix: restore only when CLI supplied none (`_option_was_provided` on all three spellings); document a clearing spelling; don't re-validate restored paths. Split out as a sub-issue #618, PR #619. Two additions to the scope: because only one of the two lists usually comes from the CLI, the merged counts disagree and `resolve_scales` pads or truncates behind a warning (`--lora-paths b` leaves `b` with no scale of its own, so the sidecar's goes to the sidecar's adapter and `b` is padded to 1.0; `--lora-scales 0.8` on a one-adapter sidecar generates at the sidecar's scale and drops the 0.8), and a sidecar from another machine exits 2 **even when the user names their own copy of the adapter**, since the dead path is merged in and resolved regardless. Kept the re-validation rather than dropping it: the next item down is that `lora_loader` prints ❌ and then reports success, so a path that skips the parser's check lands in exactly that hole — the error now names the sidecar it came from and both ways out instead. Also carved `--lora-scales` out as an independent axis, so `-C sidecar --lora-scales 0.8` re-runs the sidecar's adapter at 0.8 rather than applying a scale to nothing. Happy to switch either back.
- [x] **LoRA save path still fails silently** — `lora_saver.py:147-149` (bake exception → print → returns unbaked base into a "merged" `mflux-save` output = silent data corruption); `lora_loader.py:74-82` prints ❌ on a missing file then `:52` prints "✅ All LoRA weights applied successfully". Fix: raise / abort on failure. Split out as a sub-issue #629, PR #630. Three additions to the scope: `LoraResolution._try_resolve` **drops** an unresolvable adapter and nothing shortens the scale list with it, so `resolve_scales` pads the difference and every later adapter runs at its neighbour's strength (`--lora typo 0.3 --lora real 0.9` generates `real` at **0.3**, behind two warnings and the ✅) — that is the only one of the five reachable from a plain command line; `_apply_*_matrices_to_target` returns `False` on a target path the model lacks, a non-linear target or missing matrices, so a half-applied adapter also reports success; and `ModelSaver.save_model` bakes and saves each component in one loop, so an abort now has to come before the first file is written (it bakes everything first). Nothing that works today starts failing — a shape-mismatched adapter already errors at inference in `LoRALinear.__call__` on the same shapes, only the *bake* path skipped it silently.

### Metadata round-trip

- [x] **Embedded `negative_prompt`/`height`/`width`/`image_paths` never restored; edit CLIs can't round-trip** — embedded at `generated_image.py:224-242` but absent from the restore block (`parsers.py:386-466`): z-image/krea2 reruns silently regenerate at 1024×1024 with no negative prompt. Worse, qwen-edit/flux2-edit declare `--image-paths required=True` evaluated *before* the metadata block → `-C`-only restore **exits 2**. Fix: restore those keys behind `_option_was_provided` guards; relax argparse `required` to post-parse validation. Split out as a sub-issue #634, PR #632. Two additions to the scope: restored init images are existence-checked with the sidecar named in the error (relaxing `required` otherwise lets a cross-machine sidecar past the parser, load the whole model, and die on a bare `FileNotFoundError` at dimension resolution — the #619 treatment for LoRA paths), and the FLUX.2 CLIs now reject `--negative-prompt` on `_option_was_provided` rather than on a truthy value, or rerunning any CFG-model sidecar would exit "not supported for FLUX.2" over an argument that is nowhere on the command line. `redux_image_paths` is the same class of bug but left alone: it is embedded as `str(list_of_paths)` so it never round-tripped, and `mflux-generate-redux` does not accept `--config-from-metadata`.
- [x] **`mflux-upscale-seedvr2 --metadata` never writes the sidecar** — `seedvr2_upscale.py:110` drops the flag (sibling `flux_upscale.py:58` does it right); also excluded from the capabilities dump by `COMMAND_PREFIXES`, so #499 couldn't catch it. Fix: pass `export_json_metadata=args.metadata`; widen the capabilities prefixes. First half fixed in #604; second half split out as a sub-issue #636, PR #635. One correction to the blocker noted below: widening `COMMAND_PREFIXES` on its own would not have printed false "honored" records, because neither upscale module defines `build_parser()` — both build their parser inline in `main()`, and `describe_command` returns `coverage: "runtime-only"` with no options list at all when it is missing, which `test_every_generate_entrypoint_has_full_coverage` already catches. So the order is: adopt `build_parser()`, declare the truth, then widen. The declarations came to four flags rather than five, and one of a different kind: `--base-model` ignored on both CLIs, `--negative-prompt` ignored on `mflux-upscale-controlnet`, `--model` **conditional** there rather than ignored (a path or repo id is honored via `model_path`; only a built-in name does nothing), and `--lora` genuinely honored. `--guidance` and `--scheduler` turned out to be *never wired* rather than unhonorable — `Flux1Controlnet.generate_image` takes both and the CLI passed neither, so a typed `--guidance 6.5` was silently replaced by 4.0 — so they are forwarded, the #614 call, with 4.0 kept as the no-flag default so invocations that never set it are unaffected. That also clears the upscale CLIs off the fifth checkbox's "same false honored status still stands" note.

### Download / load integrity

- [x] **krea2 Turbo partial-download hole** — `path_resolution.py:167-188`: when `required_subdirs` is non-empty, root-level safetensors patterns are never checked. Repro: snapshot with `vae/`+`text_encoder/` but no `turbo.safetensors` → `_is_snapshot_complete` returns True → later confusing `mx.load` failure (#462 fixed subdirs only). Fix: verify root-level patterns in the subdirs branch. Fixed in #593.
- [x] **mflux-format reload ignores its own `index.json`** — `weight_loader.py:201-208` globs `*.safetensors`; a partially-copied saved checkpoint loads silently with missing tensors. Fix: validate referenced shards before loading. Fixed in #603. The parenthetical was its own bug and is split out as a sub-issue #637, PR #638: `load_single` called `snapshot_download` directly, so the FLUX and Z-Image controlnets and the Lens VAE were the only weights left that still wanted the hub with everything already cached. Note the faithful translation does not work — `PathResolution` requires every pattern to match, and two of those three repos have no root `config.json` (the Lens VAE's `FLUX.2-klein-4B` keeps its at `vae/config.json`), so carrying the old `allow_patterns` over would judge every cached copy of them incomplete and leave the named case exactly where it started.
- [x] **ernie tiled latents: non-singleton temporal data silently discarded** — `ernie_latent_creator.py` (`latents[:, :, 0, :, :]` from #463); flagged in review at merge time, unaddressed; the stricter `shape[2] == 1` gate from the orphaned #511 branch never landed (#511 merged as a byte-identical empty commit). Fix: gate on `shape[2] == 1` + add the untiled-4D test, with credit to @williamxie1989's original branch. Fixed in #587 via `latents.squeeze(2)`, which is the same gate expressed as one call.

---

Happy to split any of these into standalone issues as work is claimed — several are independent one-commit fixes. The full audit (all 45 PRs graded, P1/P2 lists, process suggestions) can be shared on request.

title: Interface consistency fixes from the growth-week audit (P1)
author: anthonywu
body:
Second tier of the growth-week audit — interface inconsistencies that are not release-blocking but will keep biting if deferred. Verified at `5c0bc14a`. See #577 for the P0 release blockers and #576 for the process gates.

**Root-cause context (same as #577):** the metadata writer (`GeneratedImage._get_metadata`, ~25 keys) and the parser restore map (~15 keys) are maintained as two asymmetric hand-written tables; `mflux-capabilities` (#499) faithfully reports whatever the parser layer does, including its misconfigurations. A single declared option↔key schema with per-key restore/override policy + a diff-scan test would close the B6–B8 class permanently.

### Lens module overhaul (largest item here)

- [ ] **Lens bypasses every module idiom** (flag half done in #579; loader half remains) — `src/mflux/models/lens/variants/txt2img/lens_image.py`: raw `mx.load` + `tree_unflatten` instead of WeightDefinition/WeightMapper, no initializer, no `CallbackManager` (so `--low-ram`, `--vae-tiling`, `--battery-percentage-stop-limit`, `--stepwise-image-output-dir` are accepted but inert), and `generate_image(..., **_ignored)` silently swallows misspelled kwargs including `scheduler` (parser accepts `--scheduler`, code hardcodes `_turbo_sigmas`). Also: `lens_generate.py:10-15` declares `IGNORED_OPTIONS` but `main()` never calls `warn_ignored_options` — the capabilities dump says "ignored" while the runtime stays silent, the exact split #499 was built to prevent. Fix: proper initializer (idioms from boogu/qwen), wire callbacks + `warn_ignored_options`, explicit kwargs. (Related P0 items in #577: mflux-save dispatch, step default.)

### Capabilities contract (#499 follow-ups)

- [ ] **Converter names leak as contract "types"** — `cli/capabilities.py:66-81`: `--vae-tile-size` → `"vae_tile_size"`, `--mlx-cache-limit-gb` → `"positive_float"`, `--height/--width` → `"int_or_special_value"`, `--controlnet-strength` → `"finite_float"` (plain `float` on the flux controlnet CLI), 69 records typed `"Path"`. Fix: explicit converter→wire-type map in `_option_type_name`; normalize `Path` → `"path"`.
- [x] **ernie-image-turbo contract self-contradiction** (done in #587) — trait says `supports_guidance: true` (from `ModelConfig`) while the CLI's own CONDITIONAL record requires guidance == 1.0 (`ernie_image_turbo_generate.py:15-20,42-44`). Derive the trait from CLI behavior, or special-case the trait.
- [ ] **Completions registry drift** — `cli/completions/generator.py:10-42` hand-maintained list has 31 of 37 scripts (missing `boogu`, `lens`, `ernie-image`×2, `ideogram4`, `capabilities`). After the P0 crash fix in #577, switch enumeration to `importlib.metadata.entry_points` (same source as capabilities) so this class of drift dies.

### Metadata writer/restore (non-blocking keys)

- [ ] **`get_right_half()` drops `negative_prompt`/`image_paths`/`redux_*` from sidecars** — `generated_image.py:75-105`; every `mflux-generate-in-context*` sidecar loses those keys, and `--save-full-image` saves pass no `export_json_metadata` (`flux_generate_in_context_dev.py:84`, `_edit.py:86`, `_catvton.py:79`). Fix: thread the fields through; pass `args.metadata` on the `_full` save.
- [ ] **`redux_image_paths` embedded as Python repr string, not JSON** — `generated_image.py:239` (`str(self.redux_image_paths)` → single-quoted repr), breaking the machine-readable sidecar contract the sibling `image_paths` (`:233`) honors. One-line fix: list comprehension.
- [ ] **Dead restore branches** — `parsers.py:448-449, 452-454`: `controlnet_save_canny` and `image_outpaint_padding` are restored from keys `_get_metadata` never writes (and the only CLI owning the canny flag takes `supports_metadata_config=False`), so #572's negative-spelling fix is only reachable via hand-edited sidecars. Fix: write the keys (and give the controlnet CLI `-C`), or delete the dead branches.

### CLI surface polish

- [ ] **Cross-family `--model` accepted without validation** — boogu/z-image/ideogram4/flux2 do `ModelConfig.from_name(args.model or default)` and proceed regardless of family: `mflux-generate-boogu --model dev` starts downloading FLUX.1-dev to run as Boogu. Lens (`lens_generate.py:36-41`) is the lone correct validator — apply its pattern.
- [ ] **Latent EXIF gap in qwen VL tokenizer** — `qwen_vision_language_tokenizer.py:81-86`: the in-memory-PIL branch skips orientation (verified: 20×40 JPEG tagged Orientation 6 stays sideways). No in-repo caller today; one-line `ImageOps.exif_transpose` future-proofs it.
- [ ] **Minor trio** — (a) in-context-edit's prompt/instruction mutual exclusion is hand-rolled in `parsers.py:511-516`, invisible to `mflux-capabilities` (use an argparse mutually-exclusive group); (b) `--width` help interpolates `ui_defaults.HEIGHT` (`parsers.py:153`, cosmetic — both 1024 today); (c) fibo-edit RMBG matte intentionally passes `export_json_metadata=False` (`fibo_edit.py:71-74`) — reasonable, but undocumented.

---

Verified-clean areas (so nobody re-hunts): baseline flag matrix on all 24 generate CLIs; kebab-case everywhere; post-#572 no un-turn-off-able restored booleans; every parser option appears in the capabilities dump; post-#571 sidecar wiring consistent across the 23 generate/concept CLIs (except seedvr2-upscale, tracked in #577).

title: Default --steps is 25 on 10 image CLIs regardless of the model
author: plz12345
body:
Split out of #577 (second checkbox under "Model registry / config resolution") so it can land on its own.

## Summary

`CommandLineParser.parse_args()` resolves the `--steps` default from `namespace.model`:

https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/blob/5c0bc14/src/mflux/cli/parser/parsers.py#L506-L508

```python
if self.supports_image_generation and getattr(namespace, "steps", None) is None:
    model_name = getattr(namespace, "model", None)
    namespace.steps = ui_defaults.MODEL_INFERENCE_STEPS.get(model_name, 25)
```

But most single-model CLIs don't choose their model at parse time — they do it in `main()`, with `args.model or "<default>"`. So at the moment this line runs, `namespace.model` is still `None`, `.get(None, 25)` misses, and the CLI inherits FLUX.1-dev's 25 steps.

The two CLIs that call `parser.set_defaults(model=...)` in `build_parser()` (fibo, ernie) are the only ones that come out right.

## Repro

Parse each CLI's own arguments with no `--steps` and read back `args.steps`, measured at `5c0bc14`:

| CLI | model it runs | `args.steps` | should be |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mflux-generate-boogu` | boogu-image-turbo | **25** | 4 |
| `mflux-generate-krea2` | krea-2 | **25** | 8 |
| `mflux-generate-lens` | lens-turbo | **25** | 4 |
| `mflux-generate-z-image` | z-image | **25** | 50 |
| `mflux-generate-z-image-turbo` | z-image-turbo | **25** | 9 |
| `mflux-generate-flux2` | flux2-klein-4b | **25** | 4 |
| `mflux-generate-flux2-edit` | flux2-klein-4b | **25** | 4 |
| `mflux-generate-qwen` | qwen-image | **25** | 20 |
| `mflux-generate-qwen-edit` | qwen-image-edit | **25** | 20 |
| `mflux-generate-ideogram4` | ideogram-4-fp8 | **25** | 20 |
| `mflux-generate-fibo` | fibo | 50 | 50 ✓ |
| `mflux-generate-fibo-edit` | fibo-edit | 50 | 50 ✓ |
| `mflux-generate-ernie-image` | ernie-image | 50 | 50 ✓ |
| `mflux-generate-ernie-image-turbo` | ernie-image-turbo | 8 | 8 ✓ |
| `mflux-generate-z-image-controlnet` | z-image-controlnet | 8 | 8 ✓ |

That is 6x the intended work on the 4-step distillations (boogu, lens, klein) and half the intended work on the 50-step base models (z-image), on the default invocation, with nothing printed to say so.

## Second, independent half: the table is keyed by alias

`ui_defaults.MODEL_INFERENCE_STEPS` is hand-keyed by *some* of each model's aliases, so spellings that `ModelConfig.from_name` accepts fall straight through to 25:

```
mflux-generate-flux2 --model flux2-klein-4b   → steps=4
mflux-generate-flux2 --model klein-4b         → steps=25    # same checkpoint
mflux-generate-flux2 --model flux2-klein      → steps=25    # same checkpoint
mflux-generate-z-image --model zimage         → steps=25
mflux-generate-qwen-edit --model qwen-edit    → steps=25
mflux-generate-ideogram4 --model ideogram-4   → steps=25
mflux-generate-boogu --model boogu            → steps=25
```

The table also has no entry at all for `lens-turbo`, and carries keys (`qwen`, `krea2`, `z-image-controlnet`, `ideogram4`) that are aliases rather than `AVAILABLE_MODELS` keys — which is what let it drift in the first place.

## Dead code this exposes

`krea2_generate.DEFAULT_STEPS = 8` is unreachable: `steps = args.steps if args.steps is not None else DEFAULT_STEPS` never sees `None`, because the parser has already substituted 25.

## Proposed fix

1. Key `MODEL_INFERENCE_STEPS` by canonical `AVAILABLE_MODELS` key and resolve aliases through the registry, so every spelling of a checkpoint shares one step count.
2. Let a CLI tell the parser which model it runs — `add_model_arguments(default_model=...)` — and use it for the `--steps` fallback.
3. Delete krea2's dead `DEFAULT_STEPS`.
4. Test that every registry model declares a step count, so adding a model without one fails CI instead of silently getting 25.

### Note on the fix sketched in #577

#577 proposed `parser.set_defaults(model=...)` per CLI. That turns out to have a side effect worth avoiding here: `namespace.model` being `None` is also the signal for "user named no model", and

https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/blob/5c0bc14/src/mflux/cli/parser/parsers.py#L536-L537

turns any `--model` value not literally present in the stale `ui_defaults.MODEL_CHOICES` into a `model_path`. Two of the defaults involved are missing from that list, so `set_defaults` would inject a broken path on the *default* invocation:

```
mflux-generate-lens --model lens-turbo        → model_path='lens-turbo'   # FileNotFoundError
mflux-generate-qwen-edit --model qwen-edit    → model_path='qwen-edit'    # FileNotFoundError
```

That is the first checkbox in #577, not this one. Keeping `namespace.model` untouched fixes the step counts without reaching into it, so the two can land independently.

title: --model and --base-model reject most built-in model names
author: plz12345
body:
Split out of #577 (first checkbox).

`ui_defaults.MODEL_CHOICES` is a hand-maintained list of accepted `--model` values that has drifted from `AVAILABLE_MODELS`. At `fc22fc6` the registry accepts 84 spellings and the list holds 24: 16 canonical keys and ~40 aliases are broken, including `krea-2-raw`, `qwen-image`, `lens-turbo`, `dev-kontext`, `ideogram-4-fp8`, and every `klein-*`, `boogu-*`, `zimage*`, `fiboedit*` spelling.

Scenario — canonical name treated as a local path
1) `mflux-generate-lens --model lens-turbo --prompt test`
2) `lens-turbo` is not in `MODEL_CHOICES`, so `parsers.py:550` sets `model_path='lens-turbo'`.
3) `FileNotFoundError: Model not found: 'lens-turbo'` — the canonical name of the only model that CLI runs.
Fix: derive the choices from `AVAILABLE_MODELS`.

Scenario — valid base model rejected by argparse
1) `mflux-generate-qwen --model some-org/some-finetune --base-model qwen-image --prompt test`
2) `--base-model` carries `choices=MODEL_CHOICES`, which lists `qwen` but not `qwen-image`.
3) Exit 2, `invalid choice: 'qwen-image'`, before `ConfigResolution` — which accepts it — is consulted.
Fix: validate `--base-model` against `ConfigResolution`'s root-model list.

Out of scope, still open in #577: family validation of `--model` (`mflux-generate --model qwen-image` builds a Flux pipeline) and `mflux-save`'s substring dispatch.

title: CLI model-choice follow-ups from #592: cache the ConfigResolution helpers, complete --base-model
author: plz12345
body:
Follow-up to the review of #592 ([@anthonywu's review](https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/pull/592#pullrequestreview-4941905190)), which approved the PR with two non-blocking nits. Filing them here rather than growing that PR's diff — neither is a regression, and #592 is a strict improvement without them.

## 1. `base_model_names()` / `base_model_keys()` rebuild on every call

`src/mflux/cli/defaults/defaults.py` caches its registry-derived helpers:

```python
@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def model_choices() -> tuple[str, ...]: ...

@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def canonical_model_choices() -> tuple[str, ...]: ...
```

The `ConfigResolution` siblings added in #592 (`src/mflux/models/common/resolution/config_resolution.py`) do not — each call re-sorts `AVAILABLE_MODELS` and rebuilds the list:

```python
@staticmethod
def base_model_names() -> list[str]:
    names = []
    for config in sorted(AVAILABLE_MODELS.values(), key=lambda m: m.priority):
        if config.base_model is None:
            names.extend(config.aliases + [config.model_name])
    return names
```

Callers today are `parsers.py:552` (once per parse) and `config_resolution.py:122` (once per explicit-base resolution), so this is not a hot path and nothing is measurably slow. It's an inconsistency, not a bug: two sets of registry-derived helpers, one cached and one not.

`lru_cache` on a `staticmethod` returning a `list` needs the return type to change to `tuple` — a mutable cached value is a footgun, and both call sites only iterate/join, so a tuple is a drop-in. `AVAILABLE_MODELS` is populated at import time and not mutated afterwards, so a `maxsize=1` cache is safe; if that ever stops being true, the `defaults.py` helpers have the same exposure and would need the same fix.

- [ ] Return tuples and wrap both helpers in `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`, matching `defaults.py`.

## 2. Wire `_mflux_models` completion to `--base-model`

`src/mflux/cli/completions/generator.py` special-cases `dest == "model"` to emit the `_mflux_models` helper:

```python
def get_value_spec(self, action: argparse.Action) -> str:
    if action.dest == "model":
        return ":model:_mflux_models"
```

`--base-model` gets nothing. Before #592 it carried an argparse `choices=` list, which the generator's generic `if action.choices:` branch would have turned into completions; #592 moved that validation post-parse, so `choices=` is gone. In practice this changes nothing — the old `choices=` list was the stale one, so the completions it produced were wrong where they existed at all — but the hook point is now free.

The natural shape is a `_mflux_base_models` helper generated from `ConfigResolution.base_model_keys()` (the canonical keys — the same short list the validation error prints, not all 84 spellings), plus a `dest == "base_model"` case in `get_value_spec`.

- [ ] Add a `_mflux_base_models` zsh helper fed from `base_model_keys()` and route `--base-model` to it.

Both are small and independent; either can land alone.

title: mflux-save writes checkpoints under the wrong architecture
author: plz12345
body:
Split out of #577 (third checkbox).

`models/common/cli/save.py:23-48` picks the save class with a substring chain over the raw `--model` string, ending in `else: Flux1`. Any name the chain has not been taught is written as a FLUX.1 checkpoint under a name that says otherwise. Nothing raises at save time — the mismatch surfaces later, as a checkpoint that will not load.

Verified at `2af8330` with every save-capable constructor mocked, so dispatch is observed without reading weights:

| `--model` | saved as | owns those weights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lens`, `lens-turbo` | `Flux1` | nothing — `LensImage` has no `save_model()` |
| `seedvr2`, `seedvr2-3b`, `seedvr2-7b` | `Flux1` | nothing — no `save_model()` |
| `klein-4b`, `klein-9b`, `klein-9b-kv` | `Flux1` | `Flux2Klein` |
| `fibo-edit`, `fiboedit-rmbg` | `FIBO` (txt2img) | `FIBOEdit` |
| `z-image-controlnet` | `ZImage` | `ZImageTurboControlnet` |
| `some-org/anything` | `Flux1` | — should be rejected |

Only the canonical `flux2-klein-*` spelling matches the `"flux2"` test; the `klein-*` aliases the registry accepts fall through to the `else`.

Scenario — a Klein checkpoint written as FLUX.1
1) `mflux-save --model klein-4b -q 8 --path ./klein-4b-q8`
2) `"flux2" not in "klein-4b"`, so the chain reaches `else: model_class = Flux1`.
3) FLUX.2 Klein weights are saved through the Flux.1 class, exit 0, no warning.
4) The checkpoint fails to load later, with no indication that `mflux-save` chose the architecture.

Scenario — an unknown name is not an error
1) `mflux-save --model some-org/an-unrecognizable-model --path ./out`
2) No substring matches; `else: Flux1`.
3) The run proceeds into a weight load rather than exiting on a name the tool cannot place.

Fix: resolve the name through `ConfigResolution` and dispatch on the canonical `AVAILABLE_MODELS` key, so canonical keys, aliases, repo ids and `--base-model` spellings agree. `parser.error()` on a name that does not resolve, and on the models that have no `save_model()` at all, rather than falling back to Flux1. A test asserting every registry entry has either a save class or a declared reason keeps the table from drifting as models are added.

Two fixes fall out of dispatching on the registry key: `dev-controlnet-canny`, `dev-controlnet-upscaler` and `schnell-controlnet-canny` currently save as bare Flux.1 (dropping the ControlNet weights) and want `Flux1Controlnet`; and `mflux-save --model boogu` dies with a `TypeError` on `bake_lora`, which `BooguImage` does not accept.

Out of scope, still open in #577: the `--model` handling on the four CLIs that ignore it, and the LoRA save path that returns unbaked weights into a "merged" output.

title: A repo id shared by two registry entries resolves to the ControlNet variant
author: plz12345
body:
Surfaced by a review comment on #607: https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/pull/607#discussion_r3790598009

`z-image-turbo` and `z-image-turbo-controlnet-union-2.1` both carry `model_name = "Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo"`. `ConfigResolution._check("is_exact_match")` and `_execute(EXACT_MATCH)` walk `base_models` sorted by `priority` and return the first entry whose `model_name` or aliases match, so the repo id resolves to whichever entry sorts first — the ControlNet, at priority 15 against plain turbo's 21.

At `2af8330`:

```
>>> ModelConfig.from_name('Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo').controlnet_model
'alibaba-pai/Z-Image-Turbo-Fun-Controlnet-Union-2.1'
```

The alias spellings are unaffected — `z-image-turbo` resolves to `z-image-turbo`, `z-image-controlnet` to the ControlNet — because neither entry lists the other's alias. Only the bare repo id is ambiguous.

This is resolver-level, so it reaches every caller that resolves a repo id, not one CLI: `mflux-generate-z-image-turbo --model Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo` builds a ControlNet config, and after #607 `mflux-save` dispatches the same name to `ZImageTurboControlnet`. The FLUX.1-dev ControlNets share a repo id with `dev` the same way and want checking under whatever rule is chosen.

Fix: make the tie deterministic on intent rather than on `priority`, which orders unrelated things. Preferring the entry with `controlnet_model is None` when several share a `model_name` picks the base variant, on the reasoning that a derived variant is always addressed by its own key or alias. Reordering the priorities instead would work but couples ControlNet selection to whatever else reads that field.

Whichever rule lands, a resolution test asserting the repo id, the canonical key and the alias all agree per model would keep it pinned.

title: Saved ControlNet weights are ignored on load; the component is re-downloaded
author: plz12345
body:
Surfaced by a review comment on #607: https://github.com/mflux-community/mflux/pull/607#discussion_r3790598010

`FluxInitializer.init_controlnet` (`flux_initializer.py:120-123`) always fetches the ControlNet component from the remote repo, ignoring `model_path`:

```python
controlnet_weights = WeightLoader.load_single(
    component=controlnet_component,
    repo_id=model_config.controlnet_model,
)
```

`load_single` takes only `repo_id` and calls `snapshot_download`. The `model_path` argument that `init()` honours for every other component is never consulted, so loading a locally saved ControlNet checkpoint silently replaces its ControlNet weights with the remote ones — a `-q 4` save reloads that component unquantized, and any fine-tune of it is discarded. It also breaks offline use of an otherwise complete local checkpoint.

Not reachable before #607: `mflux-save` dispatched `dev-controlnet-canny`, `dev-controlnet-upscaler` and `schnell-controlnet-canny` to bare `Flux1`, so the ControlNet component was never written in the first place. Those three now save through `Flux1Controlnet` and write it, at which point the loader ignoring it becomes visible.

Fix: when `model_path` is set, load the component from disk via the existing `WeightLoader.load_single_local(component, root_path)` and fall back to `load_single` only for a built-in name. A round-trip test — save a ControlNet model quantized, reload from the local path, assert the ControlNet component's quantization level matches — would cover it.

title: boogu & FIBO accept --lora then silently discard it
author: plz12345
body:
Split out from #577 (LoRA handling, first item).

### What happens

`mflux-generate-boogu`, `mflux-generate-fibo` and `mflux-generate-fibo-edit` all call `parser.add_lora_arguments()`, so `--lora` / `--lora-paths` / `--lora-scales` / `--lora-style` are accepted, the adapter is resolved and downloaded from HF (`parsers.py:538-546`), and then dropped on the floor:

- `boogu_initializer.py:38-39` hardcodes `model.lora_paths = []` / `model.lora_scales = []`.
- `fibo_initializer.py:20-21` takes `lora_paths`/`lora_scales` and never applies them. `fibo_generate.py` never forwards them; `fibo_edit.py:112` *does* forward them via `lora_init_kwargs_from_args` and still gets nothing — so **fibo-edit is affected too**, which #577 does not mention.
- `mflux-capabilities` reports `"lora": true` for all three (the trait reads `parser.supports_lora`).
- Same hole in `mflux-save`: `save.py:141-142` filters the LoRA kwargs by constructor signature, `BooguImage` accepts them, and they are ignored.

No warning anywhere — the user pays for the download and gets a base-model image.

### Fix

Stop advertising rather than implement. There are no LoRA adapters in the wild for either base (HF lists none for `Boogu/Boogu-Image-0.1-Turbo`; `briaai/Fibo-lite` is tagged `lora` but ships full merged weights, which is how mflux already loads it), and mflux has no training adapter for either family, so a mapping would be unverifiable pattern-guessing.

- Drop `add_lora_arguments()` from the three CLIs. This matches `mflux-generate-lens`, already the precedent for a LoRA-less model: no flags registered, `--help` and `mflux-capabilities` both report no LoRA support, argparse rejects `--lora` outright.
- Remove the dead `lora_paths`/`lora_scales`/`bake_lora` parameters from `BooguInitializer`/`FIBOInitializer` and the `BooguImage`/`FIBO`/`FIBOEdit` constructors, so the Python API stops lying too.
- `mflux-save`: `parser.error()` when `--lora` is given for a model whose class cannot apply it, instead of dropping it silently.
- Update the hand-maintained fibo/fibo-edit entries in `cli/completions/generator.py`.

Note on the approach: #577 suggests `REJECTED_OPTIONS`. That keeps the flags registered, so `--help`, the shell completions and the capabilities dump would all still list them, and it needs new parser machinery to reject them before the download happens. Removing them matches lens and needs none. Happy to switch if the explicit "not supported for this model" error message is worth the extra surface.

Implementing real LoRA support for these two families stays open — worth revisiting if adapters appear.

title: Non-trivial changes to Flux.1 and Fibo required to achieve CodeRabbit approval for test-tiny
author: ianscrivener
body:
Investigating doing tiny tests with Claude Code showed that some more significant changes to Flux.1 and Fibo were needed to make CodeRabbit happy. These changes will require doing full testing with Flux.1 and Fibo.

This feels like it's above my pay grade and would prefer that @plz12345 or @fxd0h take a look at this please.

<sub>Claude wrote the following PRD</sub>

--- 

# PRD: Parameterize `AdaLayerNormZeroSingle` / `TimestepEmbedder` (shared FLUX.1 + FIBO), then add tiny tests for both

## Background

`src/mflux/models/flux/model/flux_transformer/ada_layer_norm_zero_single.py` and
`src/mflux/models/flux/model/flux_transformer/timestep_embedder.py` are shared
between **FLUX.1** and **FIBO** (FIBO imports these FLUX.1 classes directly rather
than owning its own copies — confirmed via `grep -rln "AdaLayerNormZeroSingle\|TimestepEmbedder" src/mflux/`).

Both classes hardcode `dim=3072` with **zero constructor parameters**:

```python
# ada_layer_norm_zero_single.py
class AdaLayerNormZeroSingle(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(3072, 3 * 3072)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(dims=3072, eps=1e-6, affine=False)
```

```python
# timestep_embedder.py
class TimestepEmbedder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.linear_1 = nn.Linear(256, 3072)
        self.linear_2 = nn.Linear(3072, 3072)
```

This is why:
- The **FLUX.1 tiny model-saving test could not be written at all** (see
  `.claude/notes/tiny-tests.md` — FLUX.1's `T5Encoder`, `CLIPEncoder`, and
  `Transformer` all hardcode dims with no shrink knobs; this pair is part of that
  same problem, inside `Transformer`'s single-block path).
- The **FIBO tiny test** (`tests/model_saving/test_tiny_model_saving_fibo.py`,
  currently held back off `tiny-tests-2`) has to define a test-local
  `_TinyFiboTransformer` that composes FIBO's real leaf classes at toy dims — but
  these two leaves can't shrink, so they're instantiated at full production size
  (3072) inside an otherwise-tiny (dim=128) fixture. CodeRabbit flagged this:

  > `FiboSingleTransformerBlock(..., dim=128)` still creates
  > `AdaLayerNormZeroSingle()` at width 3072. `BriaFiboTimestepProjEmbeddings()`
  > also creates a 3072-wide `TimestepEmbedder`. The two single blocks and time
  > embedding add 66,871,296 parameters (~255 MiB at fp32) before the remaining
  > test components. The helper creates this fixture twice and randomizes every
  > parameter, making a "fast" test unnecessarily expensive.

Note both call sites already thread a `dim` param through everything else — they
just don't pass it to these two:

```python
# fibo/model/fibo_transformer/single_transformer_block.py
def __init__(self, layer, dim: int = 3072, num_attention_heads=24, attention_head_dim=128, mlp_ratio=4.0):
    ...
    self.norm = AdaLayerNormZeroSingle()  # <- dim not passed through
```

```python
# fibo/model/fibo_transformer/time_embed.py
def __init__(self, embedding_dim: int = 3072, time_theta: int = 10000):
    ...
    self.timestep_embedder = TimestepEmbedder()  # <- embedding_dim not passed through
```

```python
# flux/model/flux_transformer/single_transformer_block.py and time_text_embed.py
self.norm = AdaLayerNormZeroSingle()          # same issue, FLUX.1 side
self.timestep_embedder = TimestepEmbedder()   # same issue, FLUX.1 side
```

## Why this is its own workstream, not a quick fix

Mechanically this is a small, reviewable diff (add a `dim: int = 3072` parameter,
replace the hardcoded `3072` literals with it, thread it through the two callers
in each of `flux/` and `fibo/`). But `mflux` is an explicitly **line-by-line
numerical port** from PyTorch/diffusers — any change to a class in FLUX.1's and
FIBO's actual forward pass needs to be proven bit-identical at the default
(3072) width, not just "reads like a no-op refactor." That verification pass —
export-then-compare against the PyTorch reference per the `mflux-debugging`
skill — is the bulk of the real work here, not the code change itself.

## Goal

1. Parameterize `AdaLayerNormZeroSingle` and `TimestepEmbedder` with a `dim: int
   = 3072` constructor argument, defaulting to current production behavior.
2. Thread `dim` through both call sites in `flux/model/flux_transformer/` and
   both call sites in `fibo/model/fibo_transformer/`.
3. Prove numerical parity at the default width for **both** FLUX.1 and FIBO
   (not just "tests still pass" — actual tensor-level comparison against the
   PyTorch/diffusers reference, per `mflux-debugging`).
4. Once (1)–(3) land, write/restore the tiny model-saving tests:
   - **FLUX.1**: currently blocked entirely (no tiny test exists). This fix
     removes one blocker but does *not* fully unblock it — `T5Encoder` and
     `CLIPEncoder` are separately unparameterized and out of scope here. Re-run
     the `mflux-model-tiny-test` skill's blocker analysis after this lands to
     confirm whether FLUX.1 is unblocked or just less-blocked.
   - **FIBO**: re-add `tests/model_saving/test_tiny_model_saving_fibo.py`
     (currently held back on branch `tiny-tests-2`, commit removing it exists —
     recover the file from git history), update `_TinyFiboTransformer` to pass
     `dim=128` through to the now-parameterized `AdaLayerNormZeroSingle` and
     `TimestepEmbedder`, and confirm CodeRabbit's flagged param count drops
     accordingly.

## Non-goals

- Not fixing FLUX.1's `T5Encoder`/`CLIPEncoder` (separate, larger effort — no
  constructor params at all, ~4.7B and ~123M params respectively at their one
  fixed size). Tracked separately in `.claude/notes/tiny-tests.md`.
- Not touching Z-Image's or ERNIE's timestep embedders — they're already
  independently parameterized, separate classes under their own model
  directories, unaffected by this change.

## Verification plan (per `mflux-debugging` skill)

Do this for **both** FLUX.1 and FIBO, since both consume the shared classes:

1. Pick one deterministic repro per model (fixed seed, prompt, height/width,
   steps, guidance).
2. Export reference tensors from the PyTorch/diffusers side at the checkpoints
   that touch these two classes:
   - Timestep projection output → `TimestepEmbedder` output (per model)
   - `AdaLayerNormZeroSingle` output (`hidden_states`, `gate`) for at least one
     single-transformer-block, ideally the first and last
3. Run the same repro in mflux **after** the parameterization change (still at
   `dim=3072` default) and export the matching tensors.
4. Compare with `mflux-debugging`'s standard checkpoint-comparison approach:
   shape+dtype match, `max_abs_diff`/`mean_abs_diff`/`max_rel_diff` against
   `atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5` (fp32) or `atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2` (bf16/fp16) as
   appropriate, inspecting actual first-N values rather than trusting summary
   stats alone.
5. Also do one full end-to-end image generation on each model, before/after,
   same seed — confirm output images are unchanged (or diff imperceptibly
   within known fp precision noise).
6. Do **not** rely on integer-seed matching for RNG — inject the exact initial
   latents per the skill's RNG warning if any step requires seed-level parity.

Only after (3)+(5) pass for both models should the tiny tests in Goal #4 be
written/restored.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AdaLayerNormZeroSingle(dim: int = 3072)` and `TimestepEmbedder(dim: int =
      3072)` (or equivalently named param) merged, with both FLUX.1 and FIBO
      call sites passing their existing `dim`/`embedding_dim` through.
- [ ] Tensor-level parity confirmed and documented (paste the comparison output
      or a summary) for both FLUX.1 and FIBO at default width.
- [ ] End-to-end image parity confirmed for both models at a fixed seed/prompt.
- [ ] `just test-fast` / `just test` green, no regressions.
- [ ] FIBO tiny test restored and green, with the previously-flagged 3072-width
      components now actually shrunk to the fixture's toy dimensions (verify
      CodeRabbit's specific concern is resolved — recompute param count).
- [ ] FLUX.1 tiny test: re-assess blocker status; write it if now unblocked,
      otherwise update `.claude/notes/tiny-tests.md` with the narrowed
      remaining blocker (`T5Encoder`/`CLIPEncoder`).

## References

- `.claude/notes/tiny-tests.md` — coverage tracker, FLUX.1 blocker writeup,
  FIBO workaround writeup, this issue's origin.
- `.cursor/skills/mflux-model-tiny-test/SKILL.md` — tiny test pattern.
- `.cursor/skills/mflux-debugging/SKILL.md` — export-then-compare verification
  workflow to use for step-by-step parity checks above.
- CodeRabbit comment on `tests/model_saving/test_tiny_model_saving_fibo.py` in
  branch `tiny-tests-2` (PR review) — origin of this issue.
